sentences.zh: __FORCETOC__岑文本岑文本，字景仁，鄧州棘陽人。

translations.literal: Cen Wenben, courtesy name Jingren, was a native of Jiyang in Deng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Cen Wenben, whose courtesy name was Jingren, came from Jiyang in Deng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖善方，後梁吏部尚書，更家江陵。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shanfang was Minister of Personnel under Later Liang and moved the family to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shanfang had been Minister of Personnel under the Later Liang and resettled the family at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 父之象，仕隋為邯鄲令，坐為人訟，不得申。

translations.literal: His father Zhixiang served the Sui as magistrate of Handan; he was implicated in a lawsuit brought against him and could not clear himself.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhixiang served the Sui as magistrate of Handan but was sued by another party and could not vindicate himself.

sentences.zh: 文本年十四，詣司隸理冤，辨對哀暢無所詘。

translations.literal: When Wenben was fourteen, he went to the Censorate to seek redress for the wrong; in debate he spoke movingly and fluently and was never worsted.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen Wenben went to the Censorate to plead his father's case and argued with such moving eloquence that no one could refute him.

sentences.zh: 眾屬目，命作《蓮華賦》，文成，合臺嗟賞，遂得直。

translations.literal: The crowd fixed their eyes on him; he was ordered to compose the "Rhapsody on the Lotus"; when the text was finished, the whole bureau sighed in admiration, and he thereby obtained justice.
translations.idiomatic: All eyes were on him when he was told to write a "Rhapsody on the Lotus"; when he finished, the whole censorate marveled, and his father was cleared.

sentences.zh: 性沈敏，有姿儀，善文辭，多所貫綜。

translations.literal: His nature was deep and quick; he had a fine bearing, excelled at literary composition, and was broadly versed in many subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Deep and quick by temperament, he had a striking presence, wrote well, and had wide learning.

sentences.zh: 郡舉秀才，不應。

translations.literal: The commandery recommended him as xiucai; he did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: When the commandery nominated him as xiucai, he declined.

sentences.zh: 蕭銑僭號，召為中書侍郎，主文記。

translations.literal: When Xiao Xian arrogated an imperial title, Wenben was summoned as Vice Director of the Secretariat and put in charge of documents and records.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiao Xian declared himself ruler, Wenben was called up as Vice Director of the Secretariat to handle official papers.

sentences.zh: 河間王孝恭平荊州，其下欲掠奪，文本說孝恭曰：「自隋無道，四海救死，延頸以望真主。

translations.literal: When Prince of Hejian Li Xiaogong pacified Jingzhou, his subordinates wished to plunder and seize; Wenben admonished Xiaogong, saying: "Since the Sui lost the Way, the four seas have struggled for life, craning their necks to await the true lord.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Hejian Li Xiaogong took Jingzhou, his men wanted to loot. Wenben urged him: "Since the Sui lost the Mandate, the empire has been desperate for survival, all looking to a true sovereign.

sentences.zh: 蕭氏君臣決策歸命者，意欲去危就安。

translations.literal: The lord and ministers of the Xiao house who resolved to submit did so intending to leave danger and seek safety.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiao court submitted because they wanted to escape peril and find security.

sentences.zh: 大王誠縱兵剽系，恐江、嶺以南，向化心沮，狼顧麕驚。

translations.literal: If Your Highness truly lets the troops plunder and bind captives, I fear that south of the Yangzi and the mountain ranges those who were turning toward civilization will lose heart and look back in alarm like wolves and startled deer.
translations.idiomatic: If you let your soldiers pillage and seize prisoners, the lands south of the Yangzi and the Ling ranges may lose faith in the new order and panic like beasts at bay.

sentences.zh: 不如厚撫荊州，勸未附，陳天子厚惠，誰非王人？

translations.literal: It would be better to treat Jingzhou generously, encourage those not yet attached, proclaim the Son of Heaven's great kindness—who is not his subject?
translations.idiomatic: Better to win Jingzhou with kindness, rally those still uncommitted, and proclaim the emperor's bounty—who would not then be your sovereign's people?

sentences.zh: 」孝恭善之，遽下令止侵略，署文本別駕。

translations.literal: " Xiaogong approved this, immediately ordered a halt to aggression, and appointed Wenben Vice Prefect.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiaogong agreed, at once forbade looting, and made Wenben Vice Prefect.

sentences.zh: 從擊輔公祏，典檄符。

translations.literal: He followed in the campaign against Fu Gongshi and was in charge of proclamations and warrants.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the attack on Fu Gongshi and managed military proclamations.

sentences.zh: 進署行臺考功郎中。

translations.literal: He was promoted and appointed Director of Personnel Evaluation in the mobile secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Director of Personnel Evaluation on the campaign staff.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年，除秘書郎，兼直中書省。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan he was made Secretary of the Palace Library and concurrently served on duty in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 1 he became a palace librarian and also served on duty at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 太宗既藉田，又元日朝群臣，文本奏《藉田》、《三元頌》二篇，文致華贍。

translations.literal: When Taizong performed the plowing rite and on New Year's Day received the ministers in audience, Wenben presented two pieces, "Ode on the Ploughing Rite" and "Ode on the Three First Days," with splendid diction.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizong performed the sacred plowing and held the New Year audience, Wenben presented "Ode on the Ploughing Rite" and "Ode on the Three First Days," both written in rich, polished prose.

sentences.zh: 李靖復薦於帝，擢中書舍人。

translations.literal: Li Jing again recommended him to the emperor, and he was promoted to Secretariat Drafting Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing recommended him again to the throne, and he was raised to Secretariat Drafting Attendant.

sentences.zh: 時顏師古為侍郎，自武德以來，詔誥或大事皆所草定。

translations.literal: At the time Yan Shigu was Vice Director; since Wude, edicts and major documents had all been drafted by him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shigu was then Vice Director and had drafted imperial edicts and major state papers since the Wude era.

sentences.zh: 及得文本，號善職，而敏速過之。

translations.literal: When they obtained Wenben, he was acclaimed as skilled in office, and in quickness he surpassed Shigu.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wenben joined them, he was praised as outstanding in duty and even faster than Shigu.

sentences.zh: 或策令叢遽，敕吏六七人泚筆待，分口占授，成無遺意。

translations.literal: When orders and directives piled up in haste, he would have six or seven clerks dip their brushes and wait; he dictated by turns and nothing of his intent was lost.
translations.idiomatic: When edicts piled up, he had six or seven clerks ready with brushes and dictated in turn, losing nothing of what he meant to say.

sentences.zh: 師古以譴罷，溫彥博為請帝曰：「師古練時事，長於文誥，人少逮者，幸得復用。

translations.literal: Shigu was dismissed after censure; Wen Yanbo pleaded with the emperor on his behalf, saying: "Shigu is practiced in current affairs and excels at literary edicts; few can match him—may he be employed again."
translations.idiomatic: After Shigu was dismissed, Wen Yanbo asked the emperor: "Shigu knows the times and writes edicts superbly—few can equal him; please bring him back."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「朕自舉一人，公毋憂。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "I have raised up one man myself; do not worry."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor replied: "I have already found my man—you need not worry."

sentences.zh: 」乃授文本侍郎，專典機要。

translations.literal: " He then appointed Wenben Vice Director and put him solely in charge of confidential matters.
translations.idiomatic: " He then made Wenben Vice Director with exclusive charge of state secrets.

sentences.zh: 封江陵縣子。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Viscount of Jiangling County.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Viscount of Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 是時，魏王泰有寵，侈第舍，冠諸王。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Wei Li Tai was favored; his mansions were lavish and surpassed all other princes.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Wei Li Tai was then in favor, with mansions more lavish than any other prince's.

sentences.zh: 文本上疏，勸崇節儉，陳嫡庶分，宜有抑損。

translations.literal: Wenben submitted a memorial urging esteem for frugality and setting forth the distinction between principal and secondary sons, saying there should be restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Wenben memorialized urging thrift and explaining the proper limits between heir and younger sons, arguing that the prince should show restraint.

sentences.zh: 帝善之，賜帛三百段。

translations.literal: The emperor approved this and bestowed three hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and rewarded him with three hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 逾年為令，從伐遼東，事一委倚，至糧漕最目、甲兵凡要、料配差序，籌不廢手，由是神用頓耗，容止不常。

translations.literal: The next year he became Chief Minister; he accompanied the campaign against Liaodong, and every matter was entrusted to him alone—even grain transport totals, armor and weapons essentials, rationing and assignment order; he never laid down his counting rods, and thereby his vital spirit was suddenly drained and his bearing became unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became Chief Minister and joined the Liaodong campaign with sole charge of affairs, from grain shipments to arms tallies and supply allocations; he never stopped calculating, and his strength failed until his manner grew unsteady.

sentences.zh: 帝憂曰：「文本今與我同行，恐不與同返矣！

translations.literal: The emperor said in concern: "Wenben is traveling with me now—I fear he will not return with me!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said anxiously: "Wenben is with me on this march—I doubt he will come back with me."

sentences.zh: 」至幽州暴病，帝臨視流涕。

translations.literal: " When they reached Youzhou he fell suddenly ill; the emperor came to see him and wept.
translations.idiomatic: " At Youzhou he fell gravely ill; the emperor visited him in tears.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十一。

translations.literal: He died at fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 是夕，帝聞夜嚴，曰：「文本死，所不忍聞。

translations.literal: That evening the emperor heard the night watch drums and said: "Wenben is dead—this is what I cannot bear to hear."
translations.idiomatic: That night, hearing the night watch, the emperor said: "Wenben is dead—I cannot bear to hear that sound."

sentences.zh: 」命罷之。

translations.literal: " He ordered them stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered the drums silenced.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中、廣州都督，諡曰憲，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Palace Attendant and Military Commissioner of Guangzhou; his posthumous title was Xian, and he was buried with honor at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made Palace Attendant and Military Commissioner of Guangzhou, with the posthumous name Xian, and buried beside Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 始，文本貴，常自以興孤生，居處卑，室無茵褥幃帟。

translations.literal: From the first, when Wenben rose to eminence, he always regarded himself as having risen from orphanhood; his dwelling was humble and his rooms had no mats, cushions, or curtains.
translations.idiomatic: Even after he rose high, Wenben still thought of himself as an orphan who had made his way up; his home stayed modest, without fine bedding or hangings.

sentences.zh: 事母以孝顯，撫弟侄篤恩義。

translations.literal: He served his mother with filial devotion that won renown, and treated younger brothers and nephews with deep kindness and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He was famed for filial care of his mother and treated his brothers and nephews with steadfast affection.

sentences.zh: 生平故人，雖羈賤必鈞禮。

translations.literal: For old friends of his life, even if detained or lowly, he always treated them with equal courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Old friends, however poor or humble, always received his full respect.

sentences.zh: 帝每稱其忠謹：「吾親之信之」。

translations.literal: The emperor often praised his loyalty and prudence: "I am close to him and trust him."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often said of his loyalty: "I hold him close and trust him completely."

sentences.zh: 晉王為皇太子，大臣多兼宮官，帝欲文本兼攝，辭曰：「臣守一職，猶懼其盈，不願希恩東宮，請一心以事陛下。

translations.literal: When Prince of Jin became Heir Apparent, many great ministers also held Eastern Palace posts; the emperor wished Wenben to hold both offices concurrently, but he declined, saying: "I hold one post and still fear exceeding my measure; I do not wish to seek favor from the Eastern Palace—I ask to devote myself wholly to serving Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Jin became heir, many ministers doubled as palace tutors; the emperor wanted Wenben to do the same, but he refused: "One office already fills my measure—I do not seek favor at the Eastern Palace and ask only to serve Your Majesty alone."

sentences.zh: 」帝乃止，但詔五日一參東宮。

translations.literal: " The emperor then desisted, but ordered him to attend the Eastern Palace once every five days.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed but ordered him to visit the Eastern Palace every five days.

sentences.zh: 每進見，太子答拜。

translations.literal: Whenever he entered in audience, the Heir Apparent returned his bow.
translations.idiomatic: Each time he came, the heir returned his bow in full courtesy.

sentences.zh: 始為中書令，有憂色，母問之，答曰：「非勳非舊，責重位高，所以憂也。

translations.literal: When he first became Chief Minister of the Secretariat, he wore a troubled look; his mother asked him, and he answered: "I am neither a meritorious nor an old retainer; my responsibility is heavy and my rank high—that is why I am troubled."
translations.idiomatic: When he first became Chief Minister he looked worried; asked by his mother, he said: "I have neither merit nor seniority, yet bear a heavy burden at the top—that is why I worry."

sentences.zh: 」有來慶者，輒曰：「今日受吊不受賀。

translations.literal: " When people came to congratulate him, he would say: "Today I accept condolences, not congratulations."
translations.idiomatic: " To well-wishers he said: "Today you should offer condolences, not congratulations."

sentences.zh: 」或勸其營產業，文本歎曰：「吾漢南一布衣，徒步入關，所望不過秘書郎、縣令耳。

translations.literal: " When some urged him to build up property, Wenben sighed and said: "I was but a commoner south of the Han who entered the pass on foot; what I hoped for was no more than a secretary or a county magistrate."
translations.idiomatic: " Urged to amass wealth, he sighed: "I was a plain man south of the Han who walked into the capital hoping only to be a clerk or county magistrate."

sentences.zh: 今無汗馬勞，以文墨位宰相，奉稍已重，尚何殖產業邪？

translations.literal: Now, without sweat-of-horse toil, I have reached the chancellorship by the brush; my salary is already ample—why should I still multiply estates?"
translations.idiomatic: Now, without battlefield merit, I sit as chancellor by my pen alone; my stipend is already rich—why pile up estates?"

sentences.zh: 」故口未嘗言家事。

translations.literal: " Therefore his lips never spoke of household affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " He never spoke of family business.

sentences.zh: 既任職久，賚錫豐饒，皆令弟文昭主之。

translations.literal: After he had long held office, imperial gifts and grants were abundant, and he had his younger brother Wenzhao manage them all.
translations.idiomatic: In long service the court's gifts piled up, and he put his younger brother Wenzhao in charge of them all.

sentences.zh: 文昭任校書郎，多交輕薄，帝不悅，謂文本曰：「卿弟多過，朕將出之。

translations.literal: Wenzhao served as Proofreader and associated much with frivolous men; the emperor was displeased and said to Wenben: "Your brother has many faults; I shall send him out of office."
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhao was a proofreader and kept company with wastrels; the emperor told Wenben: "Your brother has gone too far—I mean to post him elsewhere."

sentences.zh: 」文本曰：「臣少孤，母所鐘念者弟也，不欲離左右。

translations.literal: " Wenben said: "I was orphaned young; the one my mother cherishes most is my brother, and she does not wish him to leave her side."
translations.idiomatic: " Wenben replied: "I lost my father early; my mother dotes on my brother and cannot bear to have him far away."

sentences.zh: 今若外出，母必憂，無此弟，是無老母也！

translations.literal: If he were sent away now, my mother would surely grieve; without this brother, it would be as if I had no aged mother!"
translations.idiomatic: Send him away and she will grieve; without him it is as though I had no mother left!"

sentences.zh: 」泣下嗚咽。

translations.literal: " Tears streamed down as he sobbed.
translations.idiomatic: " He wept aloud.

sentences.zh: 帝湣其意，召文昭讓敕，卒無過。

translations.literal: The emperor pitied his feeling, summoned Wenzhao and admonished him by edict, and in the end no fault was found.
translations.idiomatic: Moved, the emperor summoned Wenzhao and rebuked him by decree; in the end no further fault was found.

sentences.zh: 孫羲。

translations.literal: Grandson Xi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Xi.

sentences.zh: 從子長倩。

translations.literal: Nephew Zhang Qian.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Zhang Qian.

sentences.zh: 孫 羲羲，字伯華，第進士，累遷太常博士。

translations.literal: Grandson Xi, courtesy name Bohua, passed the jinshi examination and was promoted repeatedly to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Xi, courtesy name Bohua, took his jinshi degree and rose to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 坐伯父長倩貶郴州司法參軍。

translations.literal: Because his uncle Zhang Qian was punished, he was demoted to Legal Assistant in Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When his uncle Zhang Qian fell, Xi was demoted to legal assistant at Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 遷金壇令。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be magistrate of Jintan.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made magistrate of Jintan.

sentences.zh: 時弟仲翔為長洲令，仲休為溧水令，皆有治績。

translations.literal: At the time his younger brothers Zhongxiang was magistrate of Changzhou and Zhongxiu magistrate of Lishui; all had records of good governance.
translations.idiomatic: His brothers Zhongxiang and Zhongxiu were magistrates of Changzhou and Lishui, both with fine records.

sentences.zh: 宰相宗楚客語本道巡察御史：「毋遺江東三岑。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Zong Chuke told the touring censor of this circuit: "Do not overlook the three Cens of Jiangdong."
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Zong Chuke told the circuit inspector: "Do not miss the three Cens of the lower Yangzi."

sentences.zh: 」乃薦羲為汜水令。

translations.literal: " He then recommended Xi as magistrate of Sishui.
translations.idiomatic: " Xi was recommended as magistrate of Sishui.

sentences.zh: 武后令宰相舉為員外郎者，韋嗣立薦羲，且言惟長倩為累，久不進。

translations.literal: Empress Wu ordered the chief ministers to recommend candidates for Vice Director posts; Wei Silizhi recommended Xi and said that only Zhang Qian's disgrace had long kept him from advancement.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu asked ministers to nominate vice directors, Wei Silizhi named Xi, noting that only Zhang Qian's fall had long blocked his rise.

sentences.zh: 后曰：「羲誠材，何諉之拘？

translations.literal: The empress said: "Xi is truly talented—why be bound by such excuses?"
translations.idiomatic: The empress said: "Xi is plainly able—why hide behind such excuses?"

sentences.zh: 」即拜天官員外郎。

translations.literal: " She at once appointed him Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: " He was immediately made Vice Director of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 於是，坐親廢者皆得援而進矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon all who had been set back because of punished kin were able to advance by this precedent.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, officials held back by kinfolk's disgrace could advance again.

sentences.zh: 俄為中書舍人。

translations.literal: Soon he became Secretariat Drafting Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became a Secretariat drafting attendant.

sentences.zh: 中宗時，武三思用事，敬暉欲上表削諸武封王者，眾畏三思，不敢為草，獨羲為之，詞誼勁切，由是下遷秘書少監。

translations.literal: Under Zhongzong, Wu Sansi held power; Jing Hui wished to submit a memorial stripping the enfeoffed Wu princes of their royal titles, but all feared Sansi and dared not draft it—only Xi did so, with forceful and stern wording, and for this was demoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhongzong, Wu Sansi dominated court; Jing Hui wanted a memorial to strip the Wu princes of royal rank, but none dared draft it except Xi, whose language was fierce—and he was demoted to deputy director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 進吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時崔湜、鄭愔及大理少卿李元恭分掌選，皆以賄聞，獨羲勁廉，為時議嘉仰。

translations.literal: At the time Cui Shi, Zheng Yin, and Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review Li Yuanong divided control of selections; all were known for bribes, while Xi alone was stern and incorrupt, and public opinion praised and looked up to him.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Shi, Zheng Yin, and Li Yuanong then shared appointments and were notorious for graft; Xi alone was upright and won wide praise.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，詔擢右散騎常侍、同中書門下三呂。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, an edict promoted him to Right Regular Attendant of the Palace Horse and made him jointly with the Secretariat-Chancellery of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: At the emperor's death an edict raised him to Right Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and made him a joint minister of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 睿宗立，罷為陝州刺史，再遷戶部尚書。

translations.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, Xi was removed and made Prefect of Shaanzhou, then was transferred again to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong succeeded, Xi was sent out as prefect of Shaanzhou, then made Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 景雲初，復召同三品，進侍中，封南陽郡公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingyun he was again summoned as of the Third Rank, advanced to Palace Attendant, and enfeoffed as Duke of Nanyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jingyun he was recalled to the Third Rank, made Palace Attendant, and enfeoffed Duke of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 初，節湣太子之難，冉祖雍誣帝及太平公主連謀，賴羲與蕭至忠保護得免，羲監脩《中宗實錄》，自著其事。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the crisis of Prince Jiemin, Ran Zuyong slandered the emperor and Princess Taiping as plotting together; thanks to Xi and Xiao Zhizhong they were protected and escaped harm. Xi supervised the revision of the Veritable Records of Zhongzong and himself recorded this affair.
translations.idiomatic: During the crisis over Prince Jiemin, Ran Zuyong accused the emperor and Princess Taiping of conspiracy; Xi and Xiao Zhizhong shielded them. When Xi oversaw the Veritable Records of Zhongzong, he set down the episode himself.

sentences.zh: 帝見之，賞歎，賜物三百段、良馬一匹，下詔褒美。

translations.literal: The emperor saw it, sighed in admiration, bestowed three hundred lengths of goods and one fine horse, and issued an edict of praise.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read it with admiration, gave him three hundred lengths of goods and a fine horse, and issued a commendatory edict.

sentences.zh: 時羲兄獻為國子司業，仲翔陝州刺史，仲休商州刺史，兄弟子侄在清要者數十人。

translations.literal: At the time Xi's elder brother Xian was Vice Director of the Directorate of Education; Zhongxiang was Prefect of Shaanzhou and Zhongxiu Prefect of Shangzhou; brothers, sons, and nephews in select posts numbered several tens.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was then vice director of the Directorate of Education; Zhongxiang and Zhongxiu were prefects of Shaanzhou and Shangzhou; dozens of brothers, sons, and nephews held choice posts.

sentences.zh: 羲歎曰：「物極則反，可以懼矣！

translations.literal: Xi sighed and said: "When things reach their extreme they turn back—one may well be afraid!"
translations.idiomatic: Xi sighed: "When fortune peaks it turns—this should frighten us!"

sentences.zh: 」然不能抑退。

translations.literal: " Yet he could not restrain or withdraw them.
translations.idiomatic: " Yet he could not hold his kin back.

sentences.zh: 坐豫太平公主謀誅，籍其家。

translations.literal: He was implicated in foreknowing Princess Taiping's plot and was executed; his household goods were confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: For complicity in Princess Taiping's plot he was executed and his property seized.

sentences.zh: 從子 長倩長倩，少孤，為文本鞠愛。

translations.literal: Nephew Zhang Qian: Zhang Qian was orphaned young and was reared and loved by Wenben.
translations.idiomatic: Nephew Zhang Qian was orphaned young and raised with deep affection by Wenben.

sentences.zh: 永淳中，累官至兵部侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the Yongchun era he rose by stages to Vice Minister of War and Grand Councilor jointly with the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: By the Yongchun era he had risen to Vice Minister of War and Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 垂拱初，自夏官尚書遷內史，知夏官事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chuigong he moved from Minister of War to Inner Scribe and retained charge of war affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chuigong he became Inner Scribe from Minister of War, still overseeing military affairs.

sentences.zh: 俄拜文昌右相，封鄧國公。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Right Chancellor of the Directorate of Literature and enfeoffed as Duke of Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Right Chancellor and enfeoffed Duke of Deng.

sentences.zh: 武后擅位，喜符瑞事，群臣爭言之。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu usurped the throne, she delighted in portents and omens, and the ministers vied in speaking of them.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu seized power she delighted in auspicious omens, and ministers rushed to report them.

sentences.zh: 長倩懼，間亦開陳，請改皇嗣為武氏，且為周家儲貳。

translations.literal: Zhang Qian was afraid and at times also ventured to speak frankly, asking that the imperial heir be changed to the Wu clan and made heir of the Zhou house.
translations.idiomatic: Fearful, Zhang Qian sometimes urged changing the heir to a Wu prince as Zhou successor.

sentences.zh: 后順許，賜實封戶五百，加特進、輔國大將軍。

translations.literal: The empress readily assented, granted him five hundred households of substantive fief, and additionally made him Supernumerary Grand Master and Grand General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: The empress agreed, gave him five hundred taxable households, and added the titles Supernumerary Grand Master and Grand General Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 鳳閣舍人張嘉福、洛州民王慶之建請以武承嗣為皇太子，長倩謂皇嗣在東宮，不宜更立，與格輔元不署，奏請切責嘉福等。

translations.literal: Phoenix Pavilion Attendant Zhang Jiafu and Wang Qingzhi, a commoner of Luozhou, proposed making Wu Chengsi Heir Apparent; Zhang Qian said the imperial heir was already in the Eastern Palace and should not be replaced, and he and Ge Fuyuan refused to sign, memorializing for stern punishment of Jiafu and the others.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jiafu and the Luozhou commoner Wang Qingzhi urged making Wu Chengsi heir, Zhang Qian argued the heir already sat in the Eastern Palace; he and Ge Fuyuan refused to sign and asked that the petitioners be punished.

sentences.zh: 和州浮屠上《大雲經》，著革命事，后喜，始詔天下立大雲寺。

translations.literal: A monk of Hezhou presented the Mahāmegha Sūtra, setting forth the matter of dynastic change; the empress was pleased and first ordered the empire to establish Mahāmegha temples.
translations.idiomatic: A Hezhou monk presented the Mahāmegha Sūtra on dynastic revolution; delighted, the empress ordered Mahāmegha temples built throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 長倩爭不可，繇是與諸武忤，罷為武威道行軍大總管，征吐蕃。

translations.literal: Zhang Qian argued that this could not be done; thereby he offended the Wu clan, was removed, and made Grand Commander on campaign of the Wuwei Circuit to attack the Tibetans.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qian objected, offended the Wu clan, was dismissed as Grand Commander of the Wuwei campaign against Tibet.

sentences.zh: 未至，召還，下獄。

translations.literal: Before he arrived he was recalled and thrown into prison.
translations.idiomatic: Before he reached his post he was recalled and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 來俊臣脅誣長倩與輔元、歐陽通數十族謀反，斬於市，五子同賜死，發暴先墓。

translations.literal: Lai Junchen coerced and slandered Zhang Qian, Fuyuan, Ouyang Tong, and dozens of clans as plotting rebellion; they were beheaded in the market, five sons were likewise ordered to die, and the ancestral tombs were opened and desecrated.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Junchen framed Zhang Qian, Fuyuan, Ouyang Tong, and dozens of families for treason; they were executed in public, five sons died with them, and their ancestors' graves were violated.

sentences.zh: 睿宗立，追復官爵，備禮改葬。

translations.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, offices and titles were posthumously restored and he was reburied with full rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong succeeded, Zhang Qian's rank was restored and he was reburied with full honors.

sentences.zh: 附 格輔元輔元者，汴州俊儀人。

translations.literal: Appendix: Ge Fuyuan—Fuyuan was a native of Junyi in Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Ge Fuyuan came from Junyi in Bian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父處仁，仕隋為剡丞，與同郡王孝逸、繁師玄、靖君亮、鄭祖咸、鄭師善、李行簡、盧協皆有名，號「陳留八俊」。

translations.literal: His father Churen served the Sui as assistant magistrate of Shan and, with Wang Xiaoyi, Fan Shixuan, Jing Junliang, Zheng Zuxian, Zheng Shishan, Li Xingjian, and Lu Xie of the same commandery, all had renown and were called the "Eight Worthies of Chenliu."
translations.idiomatic: His father Churen was a Shan county aide under the Sui; with seven fellow natives he was famed as one of the "Eight Worthies of Chenliu."

sentences.zh: 輔元擢明經，累遷殿中侍御史，歷御史中丞、同鳳閣鸞臺平章事。

translations.literal: Fuyuan passed the mingjing examination and rose by stages to Attending Censor Within the Palace, then served as Censor-in-Chief and Grand Councilor jointly with the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyuan passed the classics examination, became a palace censor, then Censor-in-Chief and Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 既持承嗣不可，遂及誅。

translations.literal: Because he maintained that Chengsi could not be made heir, he thereby met execution.
translations.idiomatic: For opposing Chengsi as heir he was executed.

sentences.zh: 子遵，亦舉明經第，為太常寺太祝，亡命匿中牟十餘年。

translations.literal: His son Zun also passed the mingjing examination, served as Temple Invoker in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and as a fugitive hid in Zhongmou for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zun also passed the classics exam and served as a temple invoker; he fled and hid in Zhongmou for over ten years.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，訴父冤，擢累贊善大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong he appealed his father's wrong and was promoted to Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shenlong he pleaded his father's innocence and was made attendant to the heir.

sentences.zh: 輔無兄希元，洛州司法參軍，同章懷太子注范曄《後漢書》者。

translations.literal: Fuyuan had an elder brother Xiyuan, Legal Assistant of Luozhou, who with Crown Prince Zhanghuai annotated Fan Ye's Book of Later Han.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyuan's elder brother Xiyuan was a Luozhou legal aide who helped Crown Prince Zhanghuai annotate Fan Ye's History of Later Han.

sentences.zh: 虞世南虞世南，越州餘姚人。

translations.literal: Yu Shinan: Yu Shinan was a native of Yuyao in Yue Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shinan came from Yuyao in Yue Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 出繼叔陳中書侍郎寄之後，故字伯施。

translations.literal: He was given in adoption to succeed his uncle Ji, Vice Director of the Secretariat of Chen, and therefore took the courtesy name Boshi.
translations.idiomatic: He was adopted as heir to his uncle Ji, a Chen secretariat vice director, and took the courtesy name Boshi.

sentences.zh: 性沉靜寡欲，與兄世基同受學于吳顧野王餘十年，精思不懈，至累旬不盥櫛。

translations.literal: By nature he was calm and retiring with few desires. Together with his elder brother Shiji he studied under Gu Yewang of Wu for more than ten years, thinking deeply without slackening, to the point that for whole ten-day periods he would not wash or comb his hair.
translations.idiomatic: Quiet and sparing in his wants by temperament, he and his older brother Shiji trained under Gu Yewang of Wu for over a decade, applying himself so steadily that he would sometimes go ten days without bathing or combing his hair.

sentences.zh: 文章婉縟，慕僕射徐陵，陵自以類己，由是有名。

translations.literal: His writings were delicate and ornate; he admired the Deputy Director Xu Ling; Ling himself considered him of his own kind — thereby he gained a name.
translations.idiomatic: His prose was graceful and richly wrought. He admired the Deputy Director Xu Ling, who in turn saw a kindred spirit in him, and on that account his reputation spread.

sentences.zh: 陳天嘉中，父荔卒，世南毀不勝喪。

translations.literal: In the Tianchen era of Chen, his father Li died; Shinan was so broken by grief that he could not endure the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: During Chen's Tianchen reign, his father Li passed away, and Shinan was overwhelmed by grief.

sentences.zh: 文帝高荔行，知二子皆博學，遣使至其家護視，召為建安王法曹參軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen held Li's conduct in high esteem, knew both sons were broadly learned, sent envoys to their home to watch over them, and summoned him as Legal Affairs Attendant under the Prince of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen admired Li's character and, knowing both sons were deeply learned, sent officials to look after the household and appointed Shinan Legal Affairs Attendant to the Prince of Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 時寄陷於陳寶應，世南雖服除，仍衣布飯蔬；

translations.literal: At the time Ji was trapped by Chen Baoying; although Shinan had completed mourning, he still wore coarse cloth and ate plain vegetables;
translations.idiomatic: Ji was then held captive by Chen Baoying, and though Shinan had finished mourning, he continued to wear plain cloth and eat simple fare;

sentences.zh: 寄還，乃釋布啖肉。

translations.literal: when Ji returned, only then did he put aside coarse cloth and eat meat.
translations.idiomatic: only after Ji came home did he set aside his mourning garb and resume eating meat.

sentences.zh: 至德初，除西陽王友。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhide era, he was appointed Companion to the Prince of Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Zhide period he was made Companion to the Prince of Xiyang.

sentences.zh: 陳滅，與世基入隋。

translations.literal: When Chen was destroyed, he and Shiji entered Sui.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Chen, he and Shiji entered Sui service.

sentences.zh: 世基辭章清勁過世南，而贍博不及也，俱名重當時，故議者方晉二陸。

translations.literal: Shiji's compositions were clearer and stronger than Shinan's, yet he did not match his breadth and learning; both were great in name in their time, so critics compared them to the two Lus of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji wrote with a clarity and force that surpassed Shinan's, though he lacked his breadth of erudition; both men enjoyed great renown, and commentators likened them to the two Lu brothers of the Jin.

sentences.zh: 煬帝為晉王，與秦王俊交辟之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang was Prince of Jin, he and the Prince of Qin, Jun, successively recruited him.
translations.idiomatic: While still Prince of Jin, Emperor Yang—and later the Prince of Qin, Jun—both recruited him to serve.

sentences.zh: 大業中，累至秘書郎。

translations.literal: In the Daye era, he rose by cumulative appointment to Secretary Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye reign he eventually rose to the post of Secretary Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 煬帝雖愛其才，然疾峭正，弗甚用，為七品十年不徙。

translations.literal: Although Emperor Yang loved his talent, he resented his sharp uprightness and did not use him much; he remained at seventh rank for ten years without transfer.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor valued his talent but disliked his stern integrity and kept him at arm's length; he held seventh-rank office for ten years without promotion.

sentences.zh: 世基佞敏得君，日貴盛，妻妾被服擬王者，而世南躬貧約，一不改。

translations.literal: Shiji, by flattery and quick wit, won the ruler; day by day he grew noble and prosperous; his wives and concubines wore garments like a king's, yet Shinan personally remained poor and restrained — not changing at all.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji flourished through sycophantic cleverness, his household growing daily more lavish until even his wives and concubines dressed like royalty, while Shinan kept to his own frugal ways without the slightest change.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及已弑帝，間殺世基，而世南抱持號訴請代，不能得，自是哀毀骨立。

translations.literal: After Yuwen Huaji had assassinated the emperor, he killed Shiji in the interval; Shinan embraced him, weeping and begging to die in his place, but could not obtain this; from then on he was grief-stricken until only skin and bone remained.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Huaji had murdered the emperor and then put Shiji to death, Shinan clung to his brother's body, wailing and begging to die in his stead—but in vain. After that he wasted away with grief until he was little more than skin and bone.

sentences.zh: 從至聊城，為竇建德所獲，署黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He followed to Liaocheng, was captured by Dou Jiande, and was appointed Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the court to Liaocheng, where Dou Jiande seized him and appointed him Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 秦王滅建德，引為府參軍，轉記室，遷太子中舍人。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin destroyed Jiande, brought him in as staff adjutant, transferred him to secretary under the prince, and promoted him to Palace Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After the Prince of Qin defeated Jiande, he took Shinan onto his staff as adjutant, then made him chief secretary and later Palace Attendant to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 王踐祚，拜員外散騎侍郎、弘文館學士。

translations.literal: When the prince ascended the throne, he was appointed Outer Attendant Gentleman for Dispersing the Cavalry and a Scholar of the Hongwen Library.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince took the throne, Shinan was made Outer Attendant Gentleman for Dispersing the Cavalry and a scholar of the Hongwen Library.

sentences.zh: 時世南已衰老，屢乞骸骨，不聽，遷太子右庶子，固辭改秘書監，封永興縣子。

translations.literal: At that time Shinan was already aged and declining; he repeatedly begged to retire with his bones; this was not granted; he was transferred to Right Vice Tutor of the Heir Apparent; he firmly declined and was changed to Director of the Palace Library, enfeoffed as Viscount of Yongxing County.
translations.idiomatic: By then Shinan was growing old and repeatedly asked to retire, but the emperor refused. Offered the post of Right Vice Tutor to the heir apparent, he firmly declined and was instead made Director of the Palace Library and enfeoffed as Viscount of Yongxing County.

sentences.zh: 世南貌儒謹，外若不勝衣，而中抗烈，論議持正。

translations.literal: Shinan in appearance was scholarly and cautious, outwardly as if his clothes were too heavy for him, yet inwardly he was resolute and fierce; in discussion he held to the straight.
translations.idiomatic: Shinan looked the picture of scholarly modesty—so slight that his robes seemed too heavy for him—yet inwardly he was steely and unyielding, always arguing the straight path in counsel.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗曰：「朕與世南商略古今，有一言失，未嘗不悵恨，其懇誠乃如此！

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong once said: "When I discuss past and present with Shinan, if I speak one word amiss, I never fail to regret it — such is his earnest sincerity!"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong once remarked, "When Shinan and I discuss history together, a single ill-chosen word from me leaves me full of regret—that is how earnestly sincere he is!"

sentences.zh: 貞觀八年，進封縣公。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhenguan, he was advanced to enfeoffment as Duke of the County.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Zhenguan he was promoted to County Duke.

sentences.zh: 會隴右山崩，大蛇屢見，山東及江、淮大水，帝憂之，以問世南，對曰：「春秋時，梁山崩，晉侯召伯宗問焉。

translations.literal: It happened that mountains collapsed in Longyou, great serpents were seen repeatedly, Shandong and the Jiang and Huai regions suffered great floods; the emperor was troubled and questioned Shinan; he replied: "In the time of the Spring and Autumn Annals, Mount Liang collapsed; the Marquis of Jin summoned Bo Zong to ask about it."
translations.idiomatic: When landslides struck Longyou, great serpents appeared again and again, and Shandong together with the Jiang and Huai regions were ravaged by flood, the emperor grew anxious and asked Shinan what it meant. He answered, "During the Spring and Autumn period, Mount Liang collapsed, and the Marquis of Jin summoned Bo Zong for counsel."

sentences.zh: 伯宗曰：'國主山川，故山崩川竭，君為之不舉，降服，乘縵，徹樂，出次，祝幣以禮焉。

translations.literal: Bo Zong said: 'The state is master of mountains and rivers; therefore when mountains collapse and rivers dry up, the ruler for this does not hold rites, lowers his robes, rides in a plain carriage, removes music, goes out to lodge elsewhere, and offers prayer-bales with due ceremony.'
translations.idiomatic: Bo Zong replied, "The ruler is lord of the land's mountains and rivers; when they collapse or run dry, he should suspend ceremonies, wear mourning garb, ride in an unadorned carriage, ban music, move to a temporary lodging, and offer ritual prayers and gifts."

sentences.zh: '梁山，晉所主也，晉侯從之，故得無害。

translations.literal: 'Mount Liang was what Jin was master of; the Marquis of Jin followed this, and therefore suffered no harm.'
translations.idiomatic: "Mount Liang lay within Jin's domain; the marquis followed this counsel and escaped harm."

sentences.zh: 漢文帝元年，齊、楚地二十九山同日崩，水大出，詔郡國無來貢，施惠天下，遠近洽穆，亦不為災。

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Wen of Han, in Qi and Chu lands twenty-nine mountains collapsed on the same day and water poured forth greatly; he decreed that commanderies and kingdoms not come with tribute, extended bounty to all under Heaven; near and far were harmoniously at ease, and this too did not become a disaster.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor Wen of Han, twenty-nine mountains in Qi and Chu collapsed on the same day amid massive flooding. He ordered the commanderies and kingdoms to withhold tribute and extended benefactions throughout the realm; harmony prevailed near and far, and no disaster followed.

sentences.zh: 後漢靈帝時，青蛇見御坐。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Ling of Later Han, a green serpent appeared on the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ling of Later Han, a green serpent appeared on the imperial throne.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝時，大蛇長三百步，見齊地，經市入廟。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Hui of Jin, a great serpent three hundred paces long appeared in Qi territory, passed through the market and entered a temple.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Hui of Jin, a serpent three hundred paces long appeared in Qi, passed through the marketplace, and entered a temple.

sentences.zh: 蛇宜在草野，而入市，此所以為怪耳。

translations.literal: Serpents should be in grass and wilds, yet this one entered the market — that is why it was taken as an anomaly.
translations.idiomatic: Serpents belong in the wild, not the marketplace—that is why it was regarded as an omen.

sentences.zh: 今蛇見山澤，適其所居。

translations.literal: Now the serpents appear in mountains and marshes — fitting their dwelling place.
translations.idiomatic: Today's serpents have been seen in mountains and marshes, exactly where they belong.

sentences.zh: 又山東淫雨，江、淮大水，恐有冤獄枉系，宜省錄累囚，庶幾或當天意。

translations.literal: Moreover Shandong has excessive rain, the Jiang and Huai great floods — I fear there may be wrongful imprisonments and cases unjustly detained; it is fitting to review and record accumulated prisoners; perhaps then we may accord with Heaven's intent.
translations.idiomatic: As for the torrential rains in Shandong and the flooding along the Jiang and Huai, I suspect there may be wrongfully held prisoners in the jails. Your Majesty should review pending cases and release those unjustly confined—perhaps that would answer Heaven's warning.

sentences.zh: 」帝然之，於是遣使賑饑民，申挺獄訟，多所原赦。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved; thereupon he sent envoys to relieve the starving people, clarifying and reviewing court cases, pardoning many.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed. He sent officials to relieve the famine-stricken, reopened judicial review, and granted many pardons.

sentences.zh: 後星孛虛、危，歷氐，餘百日，帝訪群臣。

translations.literal: Later a broom star appeared in Xu and Wei, passed through Di, and lingered a hundred-odd days; the emperor consulted his ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Later a comet appeared in the constellations Xu and Wei, traversed Di, and remained visible for more than a hundred days, prompting the emperor to seek counsel from his ministers.

sentences.zh: 世南曰：「昔齊景公時，彗見，公問晏嬰，嬰曰：‘公穿池沼畏不深，起臺榭畏不高，行刑罰畏不重，是以天見彗為戒耳。

translations.literal: Shinan said: "Formerly in the time of Duke Jing of Qi, a comet appeared; the duke asked Yan Ying; Ying said: 'Your Lordship digs ponds and fears they are not deep, raises terraces and fears they are not high, inflicts punishments and fears they are not heavy — therefore Heaven shows a comet as a warning.'"
translations.idiomatic: Shinan said, "When Duke Jing of Qi saw a comet, he asked Yan Ying, who replied, 'Your Majesty digs ponds yet fears they are not deep enough, builds towers yet fears they are not tall enough, and punishes yet fears the penalties are not severe enough—that is why Heaven has sent a comet as a warning.'"

sentences.zh: ’景公懼而修德，後十六日而滅。

translations.literal: 'Duke Jing was afraid and cultivated virtue; sixteen days later it vanished.'
translations.idiomatic: The duke was frightened and mended morally; sixteen days later the comet disappeared.

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下勿以功高而自矜，勿以太平久而自驕，慎終於初，彗雖見，猶未足憂。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes Your Majesty not to be self-congratulatory because achievements are high, not to be arrogant because peace has lasted long; be careful at the end as at the beginning — though the comet appears, it is still not enough to worry about.
translations.idiomatic: I pray Your Majesty will not grow complacent over past victories nor grow proud because peace has lasted so long. Guard the end as carefully as the beginning, and even if the comet appears, there is little cause for alarm.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「誠然，吾良無景公之過，但年十八舉義兵，二十四平天下，未三十即大位，自謂三王以來，撥亂之主莫吾若，故負而矜之，輕天下士。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Truly so. I indeed have none of Duke Jing's faults, except that at eighteen I raised the righteous army, at twenty-four pacified all under Heaven, before thirty assumed the great throne; I considered that since the Three Kings, no lord who settled disorder was my match; therefore I carried myself proudly and looked lightly on the scholars of the realm."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "That is true. I am not guilty of Duke Jing's excesses—but I raised the army of righteousness at eighteen, brought the realm to peace at twenty-four, and took the throne before thirty. I told myself that since the Three Sage Kings no ruler who quelled chaos had matched me, and so I grew proud and looked down on the empire's men of talent."

sentences.zh: 上天見變，其為是乎？

translations.literal: Heaven shows this change — is it for this reason?
translations.idiomatic: Has Heaven sent this sign for that very reason?

sentences.zh: 秦始皇劃除六國，隋煬帝有四海之富，卒以驕敗，吾何得不戒邪？

translations.literal: Qin Shihuang swept away the six states; Sui Emperor Yang possessed the wealth of the four seas — in the end both perished through pride; how can I not take warning?
translations.idiomatic: Qin Shihuang conquered the six states, and Sui Emperor Yang possessed the riches of the four seas—yet both were ruined by arrogance. How can I fail to take warning?

sentences.zh: 高祖崩，詔山陵一準漢長陵故事，厚送終禮，於是程役峻暴，人力告弊。

translations.literal: When Gaozu died, an edict ordered that the mountain tomb follow entirely the precedent of Changling of Han, with lavish funeral rites; accordingly the projects and corvée were harsh and violent, and human labor was exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu's death, an edict decreed that his mausoleum follow the model of Han's Changling with lavish funeral honors. The construction grew brutally intense, and laborers were pushed to exhaustion.

sentences.zh: 世南諫曰：

translations.literal: Shinan remonstrated, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Shinan memorialized in protest:

sentences.zh: 古帝王所以薄葬者，非不欲崇大光顯以榮其親，然高墳厚隴，寶具珍物，適所以累之也。

translations.literal: The reason ancient emperors and kings buried sparingly was not that they did not wish to make grandeur and brightness to honor their parents; yet high mounds and thick earthworks, treasure vessels and precious objects — these precisely are what encumber them.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient emperors practiced modest burial not because they lacked desire to honor their forebears with grandeur, but because towering mounds, thick earthworks, and heaps of treasure only burden the dead.

sentences.zh: 聖人深思遠慮，安於菲薄，為長久計。

translations.literal: Sages think deeply and plan far ahead, rest content with the meager and slight, and calculate for long endurance.
translations.idiomatic: The sages looked far ahead and were content with simplicity, planning for lasting security.

sentences.zh: 昔漢成帝造延、昌二陵，劉向上書曰：「孝文居霸陵，悽愴悲懷，顧謂群臣曰：'嗟乎！

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Cheng of Han built the Yan and Chang tombs; Liu Xiang submitted a memorial saying: "Emperor Xiaowen at Baling, filled with grief and sorrow, turned to address the ministers, saying: 'Alas!
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Cheng of Han built the Yan and Chang tombs, Liu Xiang submitted a memorial citing how Emperor Xiaowen, standing at Baling, was moved to grief and told his ministers, 'Alas!

sentences.zh: 以北山石為槨，用糸甯絮斮陳漆其間，豈可動哉？

translations.literal: Using northern mountain stone for the outer coffin, stuffing chopped ramie floss between and coating it with lacquer — how could it be moved?
translations.idiomatic: Were we to seal the tomb with stone from the northern mountains, packing ramie between the layers and lacquering them—who could ever break in?

sentences.zh: '張釋之曰：'使其中有可欲，雖錮南山猶有隙；

translations.literal: 'Zhang Shizhi said: 'If within there is something desirable, even if Mount South were encased there would still be gaps;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shizhi replied, 'If there is something inside worth coveting, even a tomb sealed with Mount South would not be secure;

sentences.zh: 使無可欲，雖無石槨，又何戚焉？

translations.literal: if there is nothing desirable, even without a stone outer coffin, what worry is there?'
translations.idiomatic: but if there is nothing to tempt a thief, even without a stone coffin, what is there to fear?'

sentences.zh: '夫死者無終極，而國家有廢興。

translations.literal: 'Now the dead have no limit, yet states have decline and rise.'
translations.idiomatic: Death is endless, but dynasties rise and fall.

sentences.zh: 孝文寤焉，遂以薄葬。

translations.literal: Xiaowen awakened to this and thereupon had a sparse burial.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen took the lesson to heart and chose a modest burial.

sentences.zh: 又漢法，人君在位，三分天下貢賦之一以入山陵。

translations.literal: Moreover by Han law, while the ruler was on the throne, one-third of the tribute levies from all under Heaven went into the mountain tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han law, one-third of the empire's tribute revenue during a reign was set aside for the royal tomb.

sentences.zh: 武帝歷年長久，比葬，方中不復容物。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu's reign lasted long; by the time of burial, the central chamber could no longer hold things.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu reigned so long that by his burial the central chamber could hold no more treasure.

sentences.zh: 霍光暗於大體，奢侈過度，其後赤眉入長安，破茂陵取物，猶不能盡。

translations.literal: Huo Guang was blind to the larger principle and extravagance exceeded bounds; afterward the Red Eyebrows entered Chang'an, broke Mao Tomb and took its goods — yet still could not exhaust them.
translations.idiomatic: Huo Guang failed to grasp the larger principle and permitted excess beyond measure; later the Red Eyebrows sacked Chang'an, broke open Maoling, and plundered it for days without exhausting its hoard.

sentences.zh: 無故聚斂，為盜之用，甚無謂也。

translations.literal: To gather wealth without cause, making provision for thieves — this is utterly pointless.
translations.idiomatic: To hoard treasure for no purpose but to supply robbers is folly indeed.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝為壽陵，作終制曰：「堯葬壽陵，因山為體，無封樹、寢殿、園邑，棺槨足以藏骨，衣衾足以朽肉。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Wei built Shou Tomb and wrote a final ordinance saying: "Yao was buried at Shou Tomb, taking the mountain as the body; no piled earth or trees, no sacrificial hall or estate park; the inner and outer coffins sufficient to hide the bones, garments and coverlets sufficient to let the flesh decay."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Wei built Shouling, he issued a final ordinance: "Yao was buried at Shouling, using the mountain itself as the tomb—without earthen mounds, planted trees, sacrificial halls, or estate parks. Coffins need only hold the bones; garments need only wrap the flesh until it returns to dust."

sentences.zh: 吾營此不食之地，欲使易代之後不知其處。

translations.literal: I am planning this untilled land, wishing that after dynastic change none will know its location.
translations.idiomatic: I am choosing uncultivated ground so that after dynasties change no one will know where I lie.

sentences.zh: 無藏金銀銅鐵，一以瓦器。

translations.literal: Do not store gold, silver, copper, or iron — use only earthenware vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Let there be no gold, silver, copper, or iron—only pottery.

sentences.zh: 喪亂以來，漢氏諸陵無不發者，至乃燒取玉匣金縷，骸骨並盡，乃不重痛哉！

translations.literal: Since the chaos of mourning and disorder, none of the Han tombs has gone unopened; some even burned to take jade caskets and gold thread — bones and all destroyed — is this not pain redoubled!
translations.idiomatic: Since the years of chaos, not one Han imperial tomb has escaped looting; some were burned open for jade caskets and gold-thread shrouds until even the bones were destroyed—is that not grief upon grief?

sentences.zh: 若違詔妄有變改，吾為戮屍地下，死而重死，不忠不孝，使魂而有知，將不福汝。

translations.literal: If you disobey the edict and presumptuously make changes, I will be executed in corpse underground, dead yet dead again — disloyal and unfilial; if the soul has awareness, it will not bless you.
translations.idiomatic: If you disobey this testament and alter my burial, I shall suffer a second death beneath the earth—disloyal and unfilial—and if my spirit knows, it will bring you no blessing.

sentences.zh: 以為永制，藏之宗廟。

translations.literal: He made this an everlasting statute and stored it in the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: He established this as a permanent rule and deposited the text in the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 」魏文此制，可謂達於事矣。

translations.literal: " This ordinance of Wei Wen may be called understanding of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Wei's ordinance shows true grasp of the matter.

sentences.zh: 陛下之德，堯、舜所不逮，而俯與秦、漢君同為奢泰，此臣所以尤戚也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's virtue exceeds what Yao and Shun did not reach, yet you stoop to match Qin and Han rulers in lavish extravagance — this is why your subject is especially grieved.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's virtue surpasses even Yao and Shun, yet you would emulate the Qin and Han emperors in lavish excess—this is what grieves me most deeply.

sentences.zh: 今為丘隴如此，其中雖不藏珍寶，後世豈及信乎？

translations.literal: Now that the mound and ridge are made like this, even if no treasures are stored within, will later ages believe it?
translations.idiomatic: If the tomb is built on this scale, who in later ages will believe it holds no treasure?

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為霸陵因山不起墳，自然高顯。

translations.literal: Your subject foolishly considers that Baling relied on the mountain and raised no piled tomb — naturally high and conspicuous.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly suggest following Baling's example: rely on the mountain itself rather than raising an artificial mound, and the site will stand noble and visible of its own accord.

sentences.zh: 今所卜地勢即平，宜依周制為三仞之墳，明器一不得用金銀銅鐵，事訖刻石陵左，以明示大小高下之式，一藏宗廟，為子孫萬世法，豈不美乎！

translations.literal: The ground now divined is level; it is fitting to follow Zhou practice and make a mound three ren high; for mingqi vessels, none may use gold, silver, copper, or iron; when the work is done, inscribe stone at the tomb's left to clearly show the standard of size and height; one copy stored in the ancestral temple as an everlasting law for posterity — would this not be beautiful!
translations.idiomatic: The chosen site is level ground; follow Zhou custom with a mound three ren high. Let no grave goods be made of gold, silver, copper, or iron. When the work is finished, carve the dimensions on a stone set to the tomb's left, keep one copy in the ancestral temple, and make it a model for all generations—would that not be wise and fitting?

sentences.zh: 書奏，未報。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted; no reply was received.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted the memorial, but received no answer.

sentences.zh: 又上疏曰：「漢家即位之初，便營陵墓，近者十餘歲，遠者五十年。

translations.literal: He again submitted a memorial saying: "The house of Han, at the beginning of accession, then began building the imperial tomb — the nearest case more than ten years, the farthest fifty years."
translations.idiomatic: He submitted another memorial: "The Han emperors began building their tombs at the very start of their reigns—sometimes taking more than ten years, sometimes as long as fifty."

sentences.zh: 今以數月之程，課數十年之事，其於人力不亦勞矣。

translations.literal: Now with a schedule of mere months, imposing tasks of decades — is this not exhausting to human labor?
translations.idiomatic: To compress decades of work into a few months' schedule—is that not an exhausting imposition on labor?

sentences.zh: 漢家大郡，戶至五十萬，今人眾不逮往時，而功役一之，此臣所以致疑也。

translations.literal: In Han the great commanderies had households reaching five hundred thousand; today the population does not match former times, yet the labor projects are one and the same — this is why your subject harbors doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Han-era great commanderies held as many as five hundred thousand households, whereas our population today falls far short—yet the labor demands are unchanged. That is what troubles me.

sentences.zh: 」時議者頗言宜奉遺詔，於是稍稍裁抑。

translations.literal: " At the time commentators largely said the edict of the late emperor should be followed; thereupon the project was gradually curtailed.
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion largely favored honoring the late emperor's testament, and the project was gradually scaled back.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗作宮體詩，使賡和。

translations.literal: The emperor once composed palace-style poetry and had him continue in matching verse.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once wrote palace-style poetry and asked Shinan to compose a matching verse.

sentences.zh: 世南曰：「聖作誠工，然體非雅正。

translations.literal: Shinan said: "Your sacred composition is truly skilled, yet the form is not elegantly upright."
translations.idiomatic: Shinan replied, "Your composition is indeed accomplished, but the style is not the upright elegance befitting the throne."

sentences.zh: 上之所好，下必有甚者，臣恐此詩一傳，天下風靡。

translations.literal: What the sovereign above loves, those below must surely exceed; your subject fears that once this poem spreads, all under Heaven will be swept by the fashion.
translations.idiomatic: What the ruler loves, his subjects will surely take to extremes. I fear that once this poem circulates, the whole realm will follow the fashion.

sentences.zh: 不敢奉詔。

translations.literal: I dare not obey the command.
translations.idiomatic: I dare not comply with the command.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「朕試卿耳！

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "I was merely testing you!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I was only testing you!

sentences.zh: 」賜帛五十匹。

translations.literal: " He granted fifty bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He rewarded Shinan with fifty bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 帝數出畋獵，世南以為言，皆蒙嘉納。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly went out hunting; Shinan spoke on this matter, and all was graciously accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor went hunting, Shinan remonstrated and each time won gracious acceptance.

sentences.zh: 嘗命寫《列女傳》于屏風，于時無本，世南暗疏之，無一字謬。

translations.literal: He once ordered the Biographies of Exemplary Women copied on a screen; at the time there was no text; Shinan recited it from memory and wrote it out — not one word was wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Once ordered to inscribe the 《Biographies of Exemplary Women》 on a screen when no copy was at hand, Shinan wrote it out from memory without a single error.

sentences.zh: 帝每稱其五絕：一曰德行，二曰忠直，三曰博學，四曰文詞，五曰書翰。

translations.literal: The emperor often praised his five supreme excellences: first, moral conduct; second, loyal uprightness; third, broad learning; fourth, literary skill; fifth, calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often praised five supreme gifts in him: moral character, loyal forthrightness, broad erudition, literary mastery, and calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 世南始學書于浮屠智永，究其法，為世秘愛。

translations.literal: Shinan first studied calligraphy under the Buddhist monk Zhiyong, thoroughly investigated its methods, and was secretly beloved by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Shinan first studied calligraphy under the monk Zhiyong, mastered his methods, and was treasured throughout the world.

sentences.zh: 十二年，致仕，授銀青光祿大夫，弘文館學士如故，祿賜防閤視京官職事者。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he retired from office, was granted Silver Radiance Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; his Hongwen Library Scholar post remained as before; salary and gifts with gate guards equal to officials of the capital with active duties.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he retired, received the title Silver Radiance Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, retained his Hongwen Library scholar post, and was granted salary, perquisites, and household guards equal to an active capital official.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十一，詔陪葬昭陵，贈禮部尚書，諡曰文懿。

translations.literal: He died at age eighty-one; an edict ordered burial accompaniment at Zhaoling; posthumously conferred Minister of Rites; posthumous title Wenci.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-one. An edict granted him burial near Zhaoling, posthumously made him Minister of Rites, and gave him the posthumous name Wenci.

sentences.zh: 帝手詔魏王泰曰：「世南於我猶一體，拾遺補闕，無日忘之，蓋當代名臣，人倫准的。

translations.literal: The emperor wrote a personal edict to Prince Wei Tai saying: "Shinan to me is like one body; recovering what is lost and repairing what is lacking — not a day do I forget this; he is truly the famed minister of our age, the standard of human relations."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote personally to Prince Wei Tai: "Shinan has been to me as my own body—day after day reminding me of what I miss and correcting what is flawed. He was the great minister of our age and the moral measure of the court."

sentences.zh: 今其云亡，石渠、東觀中無復人矣！

translations.literal: Now that he has passed like a cloud, in the Stone Canal and Eastern Pavilion there is no one left!
translations.idiomatic: Now that he is gone, there is no one left in the halls of learning!

sentences.zh: 」後帝為詩一篇，述古興亡，既而歎曰：「鐘子期死，伯牙不復鼓琴。

translations.literal: " Later the emperor composed a poem treating ancient rise and fall; then sighed: "When Zhong Ziqi died, Bo Ya never again played the zither."
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor composed a poem on the rise and fall of empires, then sighed, "When Zhong Ziqi died, Bo Ya never played the zither again."

sentences.zh: 朕此詩將何所示邪？

translations.literal: To whom shall I show this poem of mine?
translations.idiomatic: To whom can I now show this poem?

sentences.zh: 」敕起居郎褚遂良即其靈坐焚之。

translations.literal: " He ordered the Diary Officer Chu Suiliang to burn it immediately at his spirit seat.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the diary officer Chu Suiliang to burn the poem immediately before Shinan's spirit seat.

sentences.zh: 後數歲，夢進讜言若平生，翌日，下制厚恤其家。

translations.literal: Several years later, he dreamed that Shinan offered forthright counsel as in life; the next day he issued an edict richly comforting his family.
translations.idiomatic: Years later he dreamed that Shinan offered frank counsel as in life; the next day he issued an edict granting generous relief to the family.

sentences.zh: 子昶，終工部侍郎。

translations.literal: His son Chang, ended as Vice Minister of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chang rose to serve as Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 李百藥李百藥，字重規，定州安平人。

translations.literal: Li Baiyao — Li Baiyao, style name Chonggui, a native of Anping in Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Baiyao, style name Chonggui, was a native of Anping in Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 隋內史令德林子也。

translations.literal: He was the son of Delin, Inner Secretariat Director of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: He was the son of Li Delin, Inner Secretariat Director under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 幼多病，祖母趙以「百藥」名之。

translations.literal: In youth he was often ill; his grandmother Zhao named him "Baiyao" [Hundred Medicines].
translations.idiomatic: As a child he was frequently ill, and his grandmother Zhao gave him the name Baiyao—"Hundred Medicines."

sentences.zh: 七歲能屬文，父友陸乂等共讀徐陵文，有「刈琅邪之稻」之語，歎不得其事。

translations.literal: At seven he could compose prose; his father's friends Lu Yi and others together read Xu Ling's writings; there was the phrase "reaping the rice of Langye"; they sighed that they could not identify the matter.
translations.idiomatic: At seven he could already compose essays. When his father's friends Lu Yi and others were reading Xu Ling and came upon the phrase "reaping the rice of Langye," they lamented that they could not identify the allusion.

sentences.zh: 百藥進曰：「《春秋》'鄅子藉稻'，杜預謂在琅邪。

translations.literal: Baiyao stepped forward and said: "In the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》, 'the Earl of Yu borrowed rice' — Du Yu says it was in Langye."
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao spoke up: "In the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》, the line 'the Earl of Yu borrowed rice'—Du Yu locates the event in Langye."

sentences.zh: 」客大驚，號奇童。

translations.literal: " The guests were greatly astonished and called him a prodigy.
translations.idiomatic: The guests were astonished and hailed him a prodigy.

sentences.zh: 引廕補三衛長。

translations.literal: By inherited privilege he was appointed Chief of the Three Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Through hereditary privilege he was appointed Chief of the Three Guards.

sentences.zh: 乃性疏侻，喜劇飲。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he was unrestrained and free, fond of heavy drinking.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was loose and free-spirited, and fond of heavy drinking.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，授太子通事舍人，兼學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, he was appointed Protocol Attendant of the Heir Apparent, concurrently a Scholar.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Kaihuang era he was made Protocol Attendant to the heir apparent and concurrently a palace scholar.

sentences.zh: 被讒，輒謝病去。

translations.literal: Slandered, he immediately pleaded illness and departed.
translations.idiomatic: When slandered, he promptly resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 十九年，召見仁壽宮，襲父爵安平公。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was summoned to an audience at Renshou Palace and inherited his father's title of Duke of Anping.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he was received at Renshou Palace and succeeded to his father's dukedom of Anping.

sentences.zh: 僕射楊素、吏部尚書牛弘愛其才，署禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director Yang Su and Minister of Personnel Niu Hong admired his talent and appointed him Vice-Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Yang Su and Minister of Personnel Niu Hong admired his gifts and made him Vice-Director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 奉詔定五禮、律令、陰陽書。

translations.literal: By imperial order he helped compile the Five Rites, the codes and statutes, and works on yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: On imperial commission he helped fix the Five Rites, the laws and ordinances, and treatises on yin and yang.

sentences.zh: 初，以疾去舍人也，煬帝在揚州，召不赴，銜之。

translations.literal: Earlier, having resigned as Palace Attendant on grounds of illness, when Emperor Yang was at Yangzhou he was summoned but did not go, and the emperor nursed a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier he had left his post as palace attendant, pleading illness; when Emperor Yang was at Yangzhou and summoned him, he refused to come, and the emperor never forgave it.

sentences.zh: 及即位，奪爵，為桂州司馬。

translations.literal: When [Yang] ascended the throne, [Baiyao's] title was stripped and he was made Marshal of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yang took the throne, Baiyao lost his noble rank and was appointed marshal of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 官廢，還鄉里。

translations.literal: When his office was abolished, he returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: After his post was abolished, he went home.

sentences.zh: 大業九年，戍會稽，管崇亂，城守有功，帝顧其名謂虞世基曰：「是子故在，宜斥醜處。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Daye, garrisoning Kuaiji, when Guan Chong rebelled he defended the city with merit. The emperor, seeing his name, said to Yu Shiji: "This fellow is still about; he should be sent to some wretched outpost."
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Daye, while on garrison duty at Kuaiji, he held the city with distinction when Guan Chong rose in rebellion. The emperor noticed his name and told Yu Shiji, "That man is still around -- he ought to be packed off to some miserable backwater."

sentences.zh: 」乃授建安郡丞。

translations.literal: " He was then appointed Assistant Prefect of Jian'an Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: " Baiyao was then made assistant prefect of Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 至烏程，江都難作，沈法興、李子通、杜伏威更相滅，百藥轉側寇亂中，數被偽署，危得不死。

translations.literal: Reaching Wucheng, when turmoil broke out at Jiangdu, Shen Faxing, Li Zitong, and Du Fuwei destroyed one another in turn. Baiyao was tossed about amid the bandit chaos, repeatedly given false appointments, and barely escaped death.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached Wucheng, catastrophe had struck Jiangdu; Shen Faxing, Li Zitong, and Du Fuwei were destroying one another in turn. Baiyao was thrown from side to side in the turmoil, repeatedly pressed into bogus offices, and only narrowly kept his life.

sentences.zh: 會高祖遣使招伏威，百藥勸朝京師，既至曆陽，中悔，欲殺之，飲以石灰酒，因大利，瀕死，既而宿病皆愈。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor sent envoys to summon Du Fuwei, Baiyao urged [Fuwei] to go to the capital. Once they reached Liyang, [Fuwei] repented midway and wanted to kill him; he was given lime wine to drink, suffered severe diarrhea, and was near death, yet afterward his chronic ailments all cleared.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor sent envoys to win over Du Fuwei, Baiyao persuaded him to go to the capital. At Liyang Fuwei changed his mind and tried to kill him, forcing him to drink lime wine; the purge nearly killed him, yet afterward every old illness left him.

sentences.zh: 伏威詒書輔公祏使殺之，為王雄誕保護得免。

translations.literal: Fuwei sent a deceitful letter instructing Fu Gongzuo to kill him, but Wang Xiongshen protected him and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Fuwei wrote under false pretenses to Fu Gongzuo ordering Baiyao's death, yet Wang Xiongshen shielded him and he escaped.

sentences.zh: 公祏反，授吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Gongzuo rebelled, [Baiyao] was appointed Vice-Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Gongzuo rose in rebellion, Baiyao was made Vice-Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 或謂帝：「百藥與同反。

translations.literal: Someone told the Emperor: "Baiyao joined in the rebellion with him."
translations.idiomatic: Someone told the emperor, "Baiyao rebelled along with him."

sentences.zh: 」帝大怒。

translations.literal: " The Emperor was furious.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 及平，得伏威所與公祏書，乃解，猶貶涇州司戶。

translations.literal: When [the rebellion] was pacified, letters from Fuwei to Gongzuo were obtained and he was exonerated, though he was still demoted to Registrar of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Once order was restored and Fuwei's letters to Gongzuo were found, the charge was dropped, though he was still demoted to registrar of Jing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 太宗至涇州，召與語，悅之。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Qin arrived at Jingzhou, he summoned [Baiyao] to converse and was pleased with him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Qin reached Jing Prefecture, he called Baiyao in to talk and took a liking to him.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年，拜中書舍人，封安平縣男。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan he was appointed Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat and enfeoffed as Baron of Anping County.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenguan he became a drafting secretary and was enfeoffed as Baron of Anping County.

sentences.zh: 明年，除禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: The next year he was made Vice-Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed Vice-Director of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 時議裂土與子弟功臣，百藥上《封建論》，理據詳切，帝納其言而止。

translations.literal: At the time there was debate over granting territories to imperial sons and meritorious ministers. Baiyao submitted his 《Discourse on Enfeoffment》, with arguments detailed and cogent; the Emperor accepted his view and dropped the plan.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated carving out domains for princes and meritorious ministers, Baiyao submitted his 《Discourse on Enfeoffment》, argued the case with precision, and the emperor took his advice and abandoned the idea.

sentences.zh: 四年，授太子右庶子。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed Right Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was made Right Attendant to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 太子數戲媟無度，乃作《贊道賦》以諷。

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent repeatedly frolicked and behaved without restraint; [Baiyao] therefore composed the 《Rhapsody Praising the Way》 to admonish him.
translations.idiomatic: Because the heir apparent kept carousing without restraint, Baiyao wrote the 《Rhapsody Praising the Way》 to admonish him.

sentences.zh: 它日，帝曰：「朕見卿賦，述古儲貳事，勸勵甚詳，向任卿，固所望耳！

translations.literal: Another day the Emperor said: "I have read your rhapsody, recounting affairs of crown princes of old and offering encouragement in great detail -- entrusting you with this duty was precisely what I hoped for!"
translations.idiomatic: On another day the emperor said, "I have read your rhapsody on the crown princes of old; the counsel is thorough, and putting you in that post was exactly what I wanted."

sentences.zh: 」賜彩三百段。

translations.literal: " He bestowed three hundred bolts of brocade.
translations.idiomatic: " He rewarded him with three hundred bolts of colored silk.

sentences.zh: 遷散騎常侍，進左庶子、宗正卿，爵為子。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, promoted to Left Attendant and Director of the Imperial Clan, and his peerage was raised to Viscount.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, promoted to Left Attendant and Director of the Imperial Clan, and his title was raised to viscount.

sentences.zh: 久之，固乞致仕。

translations.literal: After a long time he steadfastly requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: After some years he repeatedly asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗與偕賦《帝京篇》，歎其工，手詔曰：「卿何身老而才之壯，齒宿而意之新乎？

translations.literal: The Emperor once composed the 《Imperial Capital》 poems with him, admired his craftsmanship, and wrote in his own hand: "How is it that though your body is aged your talent remains vigorous, and though your teeth are long in years your mind is fresh?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once wrote the 《Imperial Capital》 poems with him, marveled at his skill, and wrote in his own hand, "How is it that your body is old yet your talent still strong, your years many yet your mind still new?"

sentences.zh: 」卒，年八十四，諡曰康。

translations.literal: " He died at eighty-four; his posthumous title was Kang.
translations.idiomatic: " He died at eighty-four and was posthumously titled Kang.

sentences.zh: 百藥，名臣子，才行世顯，為天下推重。

translations.literal: Baiyao was the son of a renowned minister; his conduct and talent were illustrious in his generation, and the realm held him in esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao was the son of a famous minister; his character and ability shone in his age, and the world held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 侍父母喪還鄉，徒跣數千里。

translations.literal: Attending his parents' funerals he returned home, walking barefoot for thousands of li.
translations.idiomatic: When he went home to mourn his parents, he walked barefoot for thousands of li.

sentences.zh: 服雖除，容貌臒瘠者累年。

translations.literal: Though mourning was finished, his face remained wasted and emaciated for years.
translations.idiomatic: Even after mourning ended, he stayed gaunt and haggard for years.

sentences.zh: 好獎薦後進，得俸祿與親黨共之。

translations.literal: He delighted in encouraging and recommending rising talent, sharing his salary with kin and friends.
translations.idiomatic: He loved to encourage younger men and shared his salary with relatives and friends.

sentences.zh: 翰藻沈鬱，詩尤其所長，樵廝皆能諷之。

translations.literal: His literary style was deep and rich; poetry was his particular strength, and even woodcutters and servants could recite his verses.
translations.idiomatic: His prose was dense and weighty, and poetry was his special gift; even woodcutters and servants could chant his lines.

sentences.zh: 所撰《齊史》行于時。

translations.literal: His compiled 《History of Qi》 circulated widely in his time.
translations.idiomatic: The 《History of Qi》 he compiled was widely read in his day.

sentences.zh: 子 安期子安期。

translations.literal: Son: Anqi -- Anqi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Anqi.

sentences.zh: 安期亦七歲屬文。

translations.literal: Anqi too could compose at age seven.
translations.idiomatic: Anqi, too, could write at seven.

sentences.zh: 父貶桂州，遇盜，將加以刃，安期跪泣請代，盜哀釋之。

translations.literal: When his father was banished to Guizhou they encountered bandits who were about to apply the blade; Anqi knelt weeping and begged to take his place, and moved by pity the bandits released them.
translations.idiomatic: When his father was exiled to Guizhou they met bandits about to kill him; Anqi knelt and wept, begging to die in his stead, and the robbers took pity and let them go.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，為符璽郎。

translations.literal: Early in Zhenguan he served as Master of Seals and Charters.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan he served as master of seals and charters.

sentences.zh: 累除主客員外郎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Vice-Director of the Ministry of Rites for Guest Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through several posts to Vice-Director of the Ministry of Rites for Guest Affairs.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，遷中書舍人、司列少常伯，數豫決國事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong ascended the throne, he was transferred to Drafting Secretary and Junior Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and often took part in deciding state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong took the throne, he became a drafting secretary and Junior Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and often helped decide state affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝屢責侍臣以不能進賢，眾不敢對。

translations.literal: The Emperor repeatedly upbraided his attendants for failing to recommend worthy men; none dared reply.
