translations.idiomatic: The emperor often rebuked his attendants for failing to recommend talent, and no one dared answer.

sentences.zh: 安期進曰：「邑十室且有忠信，天下至廣，不為無賢。

translations.literal: Anqi stepped forward and said: "In a settlement of ten households there are still loyal and trustworthy men; the realm is vast -- it cannot be without talent."
translations.idiomatic: Anqi spoke up: "Even in a hamlet of ten houses there are loyal and trustworthy men; the realm is vast -- it cannot be without worthies."

sentences.zh: 比見公卿有所薦進，皆劾為朋黨，滯抑者未申，而主薦者已訾，所以人人爭噤默以避囂謗。

translations.literal: Of late when high officials have made recommendations, [critics] denounce them as factionalism; those held back have not yet been cleared while those who recommended them are already slandered -- hence everyone strives to keep silent to avoid clamor and calumny.
translations.idiomatic: Lately whenever ministers have recommended someone, critics cry faction; the blocked man has not yet been cleared while the recommender is already attacked, so everyone keeps silent to escape uproar and slander.

sentences.zh: 若陛下忘其親仇，曠然受之，惟才是用，塞讒毀路，其誰敢不竭忠以聞上乎？

translations.literal: If Your Majesty would put aside personal likes and dislikes, accept recommendations openly, employ men solely for their talent, and block the paths of slander -- who would then not exhaust his loyalty in reporting to the throne?
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty would forget private likes and dislikes, accept recommendations openly, use men only for their ability, and shut the road to slander, who would not give his utmost loyalty in speaking to the throne?

sentences.zh: 」帝納之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 尋檢校東臺侍郎、同東西臺三品，出為荊州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Acting Vice-Director of the Eastern Chancellery, ranked equal to Third Grade of both Eastern and Western Chancelleries, then sent out as Chief Administrator of the Jingzhou Grand Defense Command.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was acting Vice-Director of the Eastern Chancellery with third-rank standing in both chancelleries, then sent out as chief administrator of the Jingzhou grand defense command.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰烈。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous title was Lie.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously titled Lie.

sentences.zh: 自德林至安期，三世掌制誥，孫羲仲，又為中書舍人。

translations.literal: From Delin to Anqi, three generations held the drafting of imperial edicts; the grandson Xizhong also became Drafting Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: From Delin through Anqi, three generations drafted imperial edicts; the grandson Xizhong also served as drafting secretary.

sentences.zh: 褚亮褚亮，字希明，杭州錢塘人。

translations.literal: Chu Liang -- Chu Liang, courtesy name Ximing, a native of Qiantang in Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Liang, courtesy name Ximing, was a native of Qiantang in Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 曾祖湮，父玠，皆有名梁、陳間。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yan and father Jie were both famous between Liang and Chen.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yan and his father Jie were both well known in the Liang and Chen eras.

sentences.zh: 亮少警敏，博見圖史，一經目輒志於心。

translations.literal: Liang from youth was keen and quick; he broadly knew maps and histories, and whatever passed before his eyes he fixed in memory.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Liang was sharp and quick; he had wide knowledge of maps and histories, and whatever he read once lodged in his mind.

sentences.zh: 年十八，詣陳僕射徐陵，陵與語，異之。

translations.literal: At eighteen he called on Xu Ling, Vice Director of Chen; Ling conversed with him and regarded him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he visited Xu Ling, Vice Director of Chen; after speaking with him, Ling found him remarkable.

sentences.zh: 後主召見，使賦詩，江總諸詞人在席，皆服其工。

translations.literal: The Last Lord summoned him, had him compose poetry; Jiang Zong and the other literati present all acknowledged his mastery.
translations.idiomatic: The Last Lord summoned him and had him compose a poem; Jiang Zong and the other poets present all marveled at his skill.

sentences.zh: 累遷為尚書殿中侍郎。

translations.literal: Through repeated promotions he became Palace Attendant in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Through successive promotions he became Palace Attendant in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 入隋，為東宮學士，遷太常博士。

translations.literal: Entering Sui he became an Eastern Palace academician, then was transferred to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui he became an Eastern Palace academician and later was transferred to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 煬帝議改宗廟之制，亮請依古七廟，而太祖、高祖各一殿，法周文、武二祧，與始祖而三，餘則分室而祭，始祖二祧，不從迭毀。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang debated altering the ancestral temple system, Liang petitioned to follow the ancient seven temples: the Founding Ancestor and High Ancestor each in one hall, following the Zhou pattern of two distant temples for King Wen and King Wu -- three together with the Founding Ancestor; the rest would be worshipped in separate chambers. The Founding Ancestor and the two distant temples would not follow successive destruction.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang debated changing the ancestral temple system, Liang argued for the ancient seven-temple plan: separate halls for the Founding Ancestor and High Ancestor, following the Zhou model of King Wen and King Wu as two distant temples together with the Founding Ancestor as three; the rest would be worshipped in separate chambers, and those three would not be subject to successive removal.

sentences.zh: 未及行，坐與楊玄感善，煬帝矜己嫉才，因是亦貶西海司戶。

translations.literal: Before this could be implemented, because of his friendship with Yang Xuangan, and since Emperor Yang was vain and jealous of talent, he too was demoted to Registrar of Xihai.
translations.idiomatic: Before the plan could be carried out, his friendship with Yang Xuangan gave cause for punishment; Emperor Yang was vain and jealous of ability, and so Liang was also demoted to registrar of Xihai.

sentences.zh: 時博士潘徽貶威定主簿，亮與俱至隴山。

translations.literal: At the time Erudite Pan Hui was demoted to Chief Clerk of Weiding; Liang went with him to Longshan.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the erudite Pan Hui was demoted to chief clerk of Weiding, and Liang went with him to Longshan.

sentences.zh: 徽死，為斂瘞，人皆義之。

translations.literal: When Hui died, [Liang] gathered and buried him; all considered this righteous.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui died, Liang gathered and buried him, and people praised his righteousness.

sentences.zh: 後為薛舉黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Later he served as Vice-Director of the Yellow Gate under Xue Ju.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served Xue Ju as Vice-Director of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 舉滅，秦王謂曰：「寡人受命而來，嘉於得賢。

translations.literal: When Ju was destroyed, the Prince of Qin said to him: "I have received the Mandate and come -- I rejoice at gaining worthy men."
translations.idiomatic: When Ju fell, the Prince of Qin told him, "I have received Heaven's mandate in coming here, and I rejoice at finding worthy men."

sentences.zh: 公久事無道君，得無勞乎？

translations.literal: You long served an unprincipled sovereign -- are you not weary?
translations.idiomatic: You long served a ruler without the Way -- are you not worn out?

sentences.zh: 」亮頓首曰：「舉不知天命，抗王師，今十萬眾兵加其頸，大王釋不誅，豈獨亮蒙更生邪？

translations.literal: " Liang prostrated himself and said: "Ju did not know Heaven's Mandate and resisted the royal army; now a hundred thousand men hold blades to his neck -- yet Your Highness spared him from execution. Would I alone not owe you a new life?"
translations.idiomatic: " Liang bowed to the ground and said, "Ju did not know Heaven's mandate and resisted the royal army; now a hundred thousand troops hold blades to his neck, yet Your Highness spared him. Would I alone not owe my life to you?"

sentences.zh: 」王悅，賜乘馬、帛二百段，即授王府文學。

translations.literal: " The Prince was pleased, bestowed a riding horse and two hundred bolts of silk, and immediately appointed him Literary Scholar of the princely establishment.
translations.idiomatic: " The prince was pleased, gave him a riding horse and two hundred bolts of silk, and at once made him literary scholar of the princely household.

sentences.zh: 高祖獵，親格虎，亮懇愊致諫，帝禮納其言。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor went hunting and personally wrestled a tiger, Liang earnestly and sincerely remonstrated; the Emperor respectfully accepted his words.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor went hunting and personally grappled with a tiger, Liang remonstrated with earnest sincerity, and the emperor respectfully took his advice.

sentences.zh: 王每征伐，亮在軍中，嘗預秘謀，有裨輔之益。

translations.literal: Whenever the Prince marched on campaign, Liang was in the army, often privy to secret plans, and contributed to his support.
translations.idiomatic: On every campaign the prince undertook, Liang was in the army, often privy to secret plans, and proved a real help.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中累遷散騎常侍，封陽翟縣侯，老於家。

translations.literal: During Zhenguan he was repeatedly promoted to Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, enfeoffed as Marquis of Yangdi County, and aged at home.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenguan he rose to Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yangdi County, and lived out his years at home.

sentences.zh: 太宗征遼，子遂良從，詔亮曰：「疇日師旅，卿未嘗不在中，今朕薄伐，君已老。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong campaigned against Liaodong, his son Suiliang accompanied him; he issued an edict to Liang: "In campaigns of old you were never absent from the center; now that I launch this expedition, you are already old."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong marched against Liaodong and his son Suiliang went with him, he sent an edict to Liang: "In past campaigns you were always at the center; now that I make this expedition, you are already old."

sentences.zh: 俯仰歲月，且三十載，眷言及此，我勞如何！

translations.literal: Looking back and forth across the years -- nearly thirty -- when I speak of this, how wearied I am!
translations.idiomatic: Looking back across nearly thirty years, when I speak of this, how weary I feel!

sentences.zh: 今以遂良行，想君不惜一子於朕耳。

translations.literal: Now that Suiliang goes with me, I trust you do not begrudge one son to me.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Suiliang goes with me, I trust you will not begrudge one son to me.

sentences.zh: 善居加食。

translations.literal: Dwell in comfort and take extra nourishment.
translations.idiomatic: Take good care of yourself and eat well.

sentences.zh: 」帝頓首謝。

translations.literal: " Liang bowed his head in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: " Liang prostrated himself in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 及寢疾，帝遣醫、中使候問踵相逮。

translations.literal: When he took to bed with illness, the Emperor sent physicians and palace envoys whose inquiries followed one upon another.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill in bed, the emperor sent physicians and palace envoys whose inquiries came one after another.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十八，贈太常卿，陪葬昭陵，諡曰康。

translations.literal: He died at eighty-eight; posthumously awarded Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, buried accompanying Zhaoling, posthumous title Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-eight, was posthumously made Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, buried with honors at Zhaoling, and given the posthumous title Kang.

sentences.zh: 遂良自有傳。

translations.literal: Suiliang has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Suiliang has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 初，武德四年，太宗為天策上將軍，寇亂稍平，乃鄉儒，宮城西作文學館，收聘賢才，於是下教，以大行臺司勳郎中杜如晦、記室考功郎中房玄齡及于志寧、軍諮祭酒蘇世長、天策府記室薛收、文學褚亮姚思廉、太學博士陸德明孔穎達、主簿李玄道、天策倉曹參軍事李守素、王府記室參軍事虞世南、參軍事蔡允恭顏相時、著作郎攝記室許敬宗薛元敬、太學助教蓋文達、軍諮典簽蘇勖，並以本官為學士。

translations.literal: Early, in the fourth year of Wude, the Prince of Qin was Grand General of Heavenly Strategy; as bandit chaos was somewhat pacified, he gathered Confucian scholars and built the Literature Hall west of the palace city to recruit worthy talent. Thereupon he issued an order appointing, while retaining their original offices, Du Ruhui, Director of Meritorious Service in the Grand Secretariat; Fang Xuanling, Evaluation Director in the Secretariat; Yu Zhining; Su Shichang, Military Advisory Inspector; Xue Shou, Recorder of the Heavenly Strategy Office; the Literary Scholars Chu Liang and Yao Silian; the Erudites of the Imperial Academy Lu Deming and Kong Yingda; Chief Clerk Li Xuandao; Li Shousu, Storage Clerk of the Heavenly Strategy Office; Yu Shinan, Recording Secretary of the Princely Establishment; the Staff Members Cai Yungong and Yan Xiangshi; Xu Chongzong and Xue Yuanjing, Director of the Office of Compilation acting as Recorder; Gai Wenda, Assistant Instructor of the Imperial Academy; and Su Xu, Military Advisory Registrar -- all as academicians in their existing posts.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, in the fourth year of Wude, the Prince of Qin held the title Grand General of Heavenly Strategy; as rebellion was partly subdued, he gathered Confucian scholars, built a Literature Hall west of the palace city, and recruited worthy men. He then issued an order naming Du Ruhui, Director of Meritorious Service in the Grand Secretariat; Fang Xuanling, Evaluation Director in the Secretariat; Yu Zhining; Su Shichang, Military Advisory Inspector; Xue Shou, Recorder of the Heavenly Strategy Office; the literary scholars Chu Liang and Yao Silian; the Imperial Academy erudites Lu Deming and Kong Yingda; chief clerk Li Xuandao; Li Shousu, storage clerk of the Heavenly Strategy Office; Yu Shinan, recording secretary of the princely establishment; staff members Cai Yungong and Yan Xiangshi; Xu Chongzong and Xue Yuanjing, Director of the Office of Compilation acting as recorder; Gai Wenda, assistant instructor of the Imperial Academy; and Su Xu, military advisory registrar -- all as academicians while keeping their original posts.

sentences.zh: 七年，收卒，復召東虞州錄事參軍劉孝孫補之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Shou died; Liu Xiaosun, Recording Officer of Dongyu Prefecture, was summoned again to fill the vacancy.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, after Shou died, Liu Xiaosun, recording officer of Dongyu Prefecture, was recalled to replace him.

sentences.zh: 凡分三番遞宿於閤下，悉給珍膳。

translations.literal: They were divided into three watches and took turns lodging beneath the pavilion; all were supplied with fine fare.
translations.idiomatic: They were divided into three shifts to lodge in rotation beneath the pavilion, and all were given fine meals.

sentences.zh: 每暇日，訪以政事，討論墳籍，榷略前載，無常禮之間。

translations.literal: On each free day he consulted them on government affairs, discussed the classics, weighed and surveyed former records, without the constraints of ordinary ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: On free days he questioned them about government, debated the classics, and sifted former records, without the stiffness of ordinary court ritual.

sentences.zh: 命閻立本圖像，使亮為之贊，題名字爵裏，號「十八學士」，藏之書府，以章禮賢之重。

translations.literal: He ordered Yan Liben to paint their portraits, had Liang compose encomia for them, inscribed their names, titles, and residences, called them the "Eighteen Academicians," and stored the set in the library to display the weight he placed on honoring worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He had Yan Liben paint their portraits, Liang write the encomia, and their names, titles, and residences inscribed; the group was called the "Eighteen Academicians," kept in the library to show how highly he valued honoring talent.

sentences.zh: 方是時，在選中者，天下所慕問，謂之「登瀛洲」。

translations.literal: At that time those chosen for it were admired and sought after throughout the realm, and the appointment was called "Ascending to Yingzhou."
translations.idiomatic: At that time those selected were the envy of the empire, and the post was called "Ascending to Yingzhou."

sentences.zh: 附 劉孝孫劉孝孫者，荊州人。

translations.literal: Appended: Liu Xiaosun -- Liu Xiaosun was a man of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Liu Xiaosun was a native of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖貞，周石臺太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhen was Administrator of Shitai under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhen served as administrator of Shitai under Northern Zhou.

sentences.zh: 孝孫少知名。

translations.literal: Xiaosun was known from youth.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaosun was known even in youth.

sentences.zh: 大業末，為王世充弟杞王辯行臺郎中。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye he served as Director of the Field Secretariat for Bian, Prince of Qi and younger brother of Wang Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Daye he served as director of the field secretariat for Bian, Prince of Qi, Wang Shichong's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 辯降，眾引去，獨孝孫攀援號慟，送於郊。

translations.literal: When Bian surrendered, the crowd drew him away, but Xiaosun alone clung to him wailing in grief and escorted him to the outskirts.
translations.idiomatic: When Bian surrendered, the others pulled away, but Xiaosun alone clung to him, wailing, and saw him off to the suburbs.

sentences.zh: 貞觀六年，遷著作佐郎、吳王友。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenguan he was transferred to Assistant Director of the Office of Compilation and Companion to the Prince of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhenguan he became assistant director of the Office of Compilation and companion to the Prince of Wu.

sentences.zh: 歷諮議參軍。

translations.literal: He served as Advisory Staff Member.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as advisory staff member.

sentences.zh: 遷太子洗馬，未拜，卒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Groom of the Heir Apparent but died before assuming the post.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed groom of the heir apparent but died before taking up the post.

sentences.zh: 附 李玄道李玄道者，本隴西人。

translations.literal: Appended: Li Xuandao -- Li Xuandao was originally a man of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Li Xuandao was originally from Longxi.

sentences.zh: 世居鄭州。

translations.literal: His family had long resided in Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long lived in Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 仕隋為齊王府屬。

translations.literal: He served Sui as an aide in the Princely Establishment of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui he served as an aide in the household of the Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 李密據洛口，署記室。

translations.literal: When Li Mi held Luokou, [Xuandao] was appointed Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Mi held Luokou, Xuandao was made his recorder.

sentences.zh: 密敗，為王世充所執，眾懼不能寐，獨玄道曰：「死生有命，憂能了乎？

translations.literal: When Mi was defeated, [Xuandao] was seized by Wang Shichong; the crowd feared and could not sleep, but Xuandao alone said: "Life and death are ordained -- can worry finish the matter?"
translations.idiomatic: When Mi fell, Xuandao was taken by Wang Shichong; the others were too afraid to sleep, but Xuandao alone said, "Life and death are fated -- can worry settle anything?"

sentences.zh: 」寢甚安。

translations.literal: " He slept very peacefully.
translations.idiomatic: " He slept soundly.

sentences.zh: 及見世充，辭色不撓，釋縛，為著作佐郎。

translations.literal: When he was brought before Shichong, his words and demeanor did not waver; [Shichong] released his bonds and made him Assistant Director of the Office of Compilation.
translations.idiomatic: When he was brought before Shichong, his words and bearing did not falter; Shichong freed him and made him assistant director of the Office of Compilation.

sentences.zh: 東都平，為秦王府主簿。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Capital was pacified, he became Chief Clerk of the Prince of Qin's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: After the Eastern Capital was pacified, he became chief clerk of the Prince of Qin's household.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，累遷給事中，姑臧縣男。

translations.literal: Early in Zhenguan he was repeatedly promoted to Supervising Censor and enfeoffed as Baron of Guzang County.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan he rose to supervising censor and was enfeoffed as Baron of Guzang County.

sentences.zh: 出為幽州長史，佐都督王君廓，專持府事。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Chief Administrator of Youzhou, assisting the Area Commander Wang Junkuo and holding sole charge of the command's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as chief administrator of You Prefecture, assisting Area Commander Wang Junkuo and running the command's affairs himself.

sentences.zh: 君廓不法，每以義裁糾之。

translations.literal: Junkuo acted unlawfully, and [Xuandao] repeatedly checked him by right principle.
translations.idiomatic: Junkuo broke the law, and Xuandao repeatedly corrected him on grounds of principle.

sentences.zh: 嘗遺玄道婢，乃良家子為所掠，遣去不納，由是始隙。

translations.literal: Once [Junkuo] sent Xuandao a maidservant who was in fact a respectable family's daughter whom he had seized; Xuandao sent her away and would not accept her, and from this their rift began.
translations.idiomatic: Once Junkuo sent Xuandao a maidservant who turned out to be a good family's daughter he had seized; Xuandao sent her back and refused the gift, and from that their breach began.

sentences.zh: 君廓入朝，玄道寓書房玄齡，玄齡本甥也。

translations.literal: Junkuo went to court; Xuandao was lodging at the house of Fang Xuanling -- Xuanling was his nephew by birth.
translations.idiomatic: When Junkuo went to court, Xuandao was staying with Fang Xuanling, who was his nephew.

sentences.zh: 君廓發其書，不識草字，疑以謀己，遂反。

translations.literal: Junkuo opened the letter, could not read cursive script, suspected a plot against himself, and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Junkuo opened the letter, could not decipher the cursive hand, suspected a plot against him, and rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 坐是流巂州，未幾，擢常州刺史，風績清簡，下詔褒美，賜繒帛。

translations.literal: For this [Xuandao] was exiled to Juan Prefecture; before long he was promoted to prefect of Changzhou; his governance was clear and plain; an edict praised him and granted silk.
translations.idiomatic: For this Xuandao was banished to Juan Prefecture; soon after he was promoted to prefect of Changzhou, where his rule was clear and spare; the throne issued a decree of praise and granted him silk.

sentences.zh: 久之，致仕，加銀青光祿大夫，以祿歸第，卒。

translations.literal: After a long time he retired; was given the title Silver Gleaming Grand Master for Splendid Happiness; returned home on his salary; and died.
translations.idiomatic: In time he retired, was made Silver Gleaming Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, went home on his stipend, and died.

sentences.zh: 附 李守素李守素者，趙州人。

translations.literal: Appendix: Li Shousu. Li Shousu was a man of Zhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Li Shousu. Li Shousu came from Zhao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 王世充平，召署天策府倉曹參軍，通氏姓學，世號「肉譜」。

translations.literal: When Wang Shichong was pacified, [Li] was summoned and appointed Warehouse Clerk in the Celestial Stratagem Office; versed in the study of surnames and clans, the age styled him the "Meat Genealogy."
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Shichong was subdued, Li was summoned and made warehouse clerk in the Celestial Stratagem Office; expert in clan and surname lore, his age called him the "Meat Genealogy."

sentences.zh: 虞世南與論人物，始言江左、山東，尚相酬對；

translations.literal: Yu Shinan discussed with him the evaluation of men; at first speaking of the Jiangzuo and Shandong regions, they still matched wits in reply;
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shinan debated men of talent with him; when they began with the Jiangzuo and Shandong regions, they could still hold their own in exchange;

sentences.zh: 至北地，則笑而不答，歎曰：「肉譜定可畏。

translations.literal: when it came to the northern regions, [Shousu] merely laughed and did not answer; [Shinan] sighed and said: "The Meat Genealogy is truly formidable.
translations.idiomatic: but when the talk turned to the north, Shousu only laughed and kept silent; Shinan sighed and said, "The Meat Genealogy is truly formidable.

sentences.zh: 」許敬宗曰：「倉曹此名，豈雅目邪？

translations.literal: " Xu Jingzong said: "This name for the warehouse clerk -- is it an elegant title?
translations.idiomatic: " Xu Jingzong said, "This nickname for the warehouse clerk -- is it a refined one?

sentences.zh: 宜有以更之。

translations.literal: There ought to be something to replace it.
translations.idiomatic: Surely something better ought to replace it.

sentences.zh: 」世南曰：「昔任彥升通經，時稱'五經笥'，今以倉曹為'人物志'，可乎？

translations.literal: " Shinan said: "In former times Ren Yansheng mastered the classics and was styled the 'Casket of the Five Classics'; might we style the warehouse clerk the 'Record of Persons' -- would that do?
translations.idiomatic: " Shinan said, "In olden days Ren Yansheng mastered the classics and was called the 'Casket of the Five Classics'; might we call the warehouse clerk the 'Record of Persons' -- would that serve?

sentences.zh: 」時渭州刺史李淹亦明譜學，守素所論，惟淹能抗之。

translations.literal: " At that time Li Yan, prefect of Wei Prefecture, was also versed in genealogical studies; of Shousu's disquisitions, only Yan could contend with him.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time Li Yan, prefect of Wei Prefecture, was also learned in genealogy; of Shousu's arguments, only Yan could stand against him.

sentences.zh: 姚思廉姚思廉，本名簡，以字行，陳吏部尚書察之子。

translations.literal: Yao Silian. Yao Silian, original name Jian, used his courtesy name in public; he was the son of Yao Cha, Minister of Personnel under Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Silian. Yao Silian, whose original name was Jian, went by his courtesy name; he was the son of Yao Cha, Minister of Personnel under Chen.

sentences.zh: 陳亡，察自吳興遷京兆，遂為萬年人。

translations.literal: When Chen fell, Cha moved from Wuxing to Jingzhao and thus became a man of Wannian.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell, Cha moved from Wuxing to the capital district and became a man of Wannian.

sentences.zh: 思廉少受《漢書》於察，盡傳其業。

translations.literal: Silian in youth received the 《Book of Han》 from Cha and fully inherited his work.
translations.idiomatic: Silian studied the 《Book of Han》 under Cha in his youth and wholly inherited his father's craft.

sentences.zh: 寡嗜欲，惟一於學，未嘗問家人生貲。

translations.literal: He had few desires, devoted himself solely to learning, and never inquired after his household's livelihood or property.
translations.idiomatic: He cared little for pleasure, gave himself wholly to study, and never once asked after his family's means.

sentences.zh: 仕陳會稽王主簿。

translations.literal: He served Chen as chief clerk to the Prince of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chen he served as chief clerk to the Prince of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 入隋，為漢王府參軍事，以父喪免。

translations.literal: Entering Sui, he became military adjutant in the Princely Establishment of Han; he was dismissed on account of his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui he became military adjutant in the household of the Prince of Han and was dismissed when his father died.

sentences.zh: 服除，補河間郡司法書佐。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was appointed legal clerk of Hejian Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After his mourning period ended, he was posted as legal clerk of Hejian Commandery.

sentences.zh: 初，察在陳，嘗脩梁、陳二史，未就，死，以屬思廉，故思廉表父遺言，有詔聽續。

translations.literal: Initially, while Cha was in Chen, he had begun compiling the histories of Liang and Chen but had not finished when he died; he entrusted the task to Silian, so Silian memorialized his father's dying charge, and an edict permitted him to continue.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while serving Chen, Cha had begun the histories of Liang and Chen but died before finishing; he left the work to Silian, who memorialized his father's dying wish, and an edict allowed him to continue.

sentences.zh: 煬帝又詔與起居舍人崔祖浚脩《區宇圖志》。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang also ordered him, together with Diarist Cui Zujun, to compile the 《Gazetteer of the Realm》.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang also ordered him and diarist Cui Zujun to compile the 《Gazetteer of the Realm》.

sentences.zh: 遷代王侍讀。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be reader-in-waiting to the Prince of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as reader to the Prince of Dai.

sentences.zh: 高祖定京師，府僚皆奔亡，獨思廉侍王，兵將升殿，思廉厲聲曰：「唐公起義，本安王室，若等不宜無禮于王。

translations.literal: When Gaozu secured the capital, the princely staff all fled; Silian alone attended the prince. As troops were about to ascend the hall, Silian said sharply: "The Duke of Tang raised his army to secure the imperial house; you ought not show disrespect to the prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the capital, every member of the princely household fled except Silian, who stayed with the prince. As soldiers were about to enter the hall, Silian cried out, "The Duke of Tang took up arms to restore the throne; you must not treat the prince with disrespect.

sentences.zh: 」眾眙卻，布列階下。

translations.literal: " The crowd stared and fell back, arraying themselves below the steps.
translations.idiomatic: " The soldiers stared, fell back, and formed ranks below the steps.

sentences.zh: 帝義之，聽扶王至順陽閤，泣辭去。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved his conduct, permitted him to support the prince to Shunyang Pavilion, and took leave in tears.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor admired his loyalty, allowed him to escort the prince to Shunyang Pavilion, and left in tears.

sentences.zh: 觀者歎曰：「仁者有勇，謂此人乎！

translations.literal: Onlookers sighed and said: "The benevolent also have courage -- is this not the man?
translations.idiomatic: Those who watched sighed and said, "The benevolent can also be brave -- they must have meant this man!

sentences.zh: 」俄授秦王府文學。

translations.literal: " Soon after he was appointed Literary Instructor in the Prince of Qin's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon afterward he was made literary instructor in the Prince of Qin's household.

sentences.zh: 王討徐圓朗，嘗語隋事，慨然歎曰：「姚思廉蒙素刃以明大節，古所難者。

translations.literal: When the Prince campaigned against Xu Yuanlang, he once spoke of Sui affairs and sighed with feeling: "Yao Silian bore the naked blade to declare great integrity -- a thing hard to find in antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince campaigned against Xu Yuanlang, he once spoke of Sui times and sighed, "Yao Silian faced the naked blade to prove his great integrity -- a thing rarely seen in olden days.

sentences.zh: 」時思廉在洛陽，遣使遺物三百段，致書曰：「景想節義，故有是贈。

translations.literal: " At that time Silian was in Luoyang; [the Prince] sent an envoy with a gift of three hundred bolts of goods and a letter saying: "I think on your integrity and righteousness, and therefore make this gift
translations.idiomatic: " Silian was then in Luoyang; the prince sent an envoy with three hundred bolts of goods and a letter saying, "I have long admired your integrity, and so send this gift

sentences.zh: 王為皇太子，遷洗馬。

translations.literal: When the Prince became crown prince, [Silian] was transferred to Cavalry Escort.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince became heir apparent, Silian was made his cavalry escort.

sentences.zh: 即位，改著作郎、弘文館學士。

translations.literal: When [the Prince] acceded to the throne, [Silian] was made Director of the Office of Compilation and a scholar of the Hongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When he took the throne, Silian became director of the Office of Compilation and a scholar of the Hongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 詔與魏征共撰《梁》、《陳書》，思廉采謝炅、顧野王等諸家言，推究綜括，為梁、陳二家史，以卒父業。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to compile with Wei Zheng the 《Book of Liang》 and 《Book of Chen》; Silian gathered the statements of Xie Huan, Gu Yewang, and other schools, investigated and synthesized them, and made the two histories of Liang and Chen, thereby completing his father's work.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him and Wei Zheng to compile the 《Book of Liang》 and 《Book of Chen》; Silian drew on Xie Huan, Gu Yewang, and other sources, sifted and synthesized them into the two histories, and so finished his father's work.

sentences.zh: 賜雜彩五百段，加通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was granted five hundred bolts of variegated silk and promoted to General Gentleman of Comprehensive Directness and Regular Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He received five hundred bolts of variegated silk and was promoted to general gentleman of comprehensive directness and regular cavalry.

sentences.zh: 以籓邸恩，凡政事得失，許密以聞，思廉亦展盡無所諱。

translations.literal: In return for favor from the princely household, he was permitted to report privately on the gains and losses of government affairs; Silian too laid everything out without concealment.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his old ties to the princely household, he was allowed to report privately on the rights and wrongs of policy, and Silian held nothing back.

sentences.zh: 帝幸九成宮，思廉以為「離宮游幸是秦皇、漢武事，非堯、舜、禹、湯所為」。

translations.literal: When the Emperor visited Jiucheng Palace, Silian held that "resort to detached palaces for pleasure touring was the way of Qin Shihuang and Han Wudi, not what Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang did."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited Jiucheng Palace, Silian argued that "pleasure tours to detached palaces were the ways of Qin Shihuang and Han Wudi, not of Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang."

sentences.zh: 帝諭曰：「朕嘗苦氣疾，熱即頓劇，豈為遊賞者乎？

translations.literal: The Emperor instructed him: "I have long suffered from qing illness; when it heats up the affliction grows sharp -- would I do this for mere sightseeing?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "I have long suffered from qi illness; when the heat comes on it turns severe -- do you think I am doing this for pleasure?

sentences.zh: 」賜帛五十匹，拜散騎常侍、豐城縣男。

translations.literal: " He was granted fifty bolts of silk and appointed Regular Cavalry Attendant and Baron of Fengcheng County.
translations.idiomatic: " He was given fifty bolts of silk and appointed regular cavalry attendant and Baron of Fengcheng County.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太常卿，諡曰康，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: He died; was posthumously made Minister of Imperial Sacrifices; given the posthumous name Kang; and buried at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: He died, was posthumously made Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, given the posthumous name Kang, and buried at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 孫璹。

translations.literal: His grandson was Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He had a grandson named Shu.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：隋煬帝失德，高祖總豪英，興北方，鼓行入關，舉京師，轟若震霆。

translations.literal: A eulogy says: Sui Emperor Yang lost virtue; Gaozu rallied heroes and worthies, rose in the north, marched drum-beating through the passes, seized the capital -- thunderous as shaken lightning.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogy says: Sui Emperor Yang lost the Way; Gaozu gathered heroes, rose in the north, marched with drums through the passes, took the capital, and shook the realm like thunder.

sentences.zh: 思廉以諸生侍孱王，奮然陳大義，挫虓虎而奪之氣，勇夫悍心，褫駭自卻，不敢加無禮於其君。

translations.literal: Silian, a mere student, attended a feeble prince; yet boldly he stated the great principle, blunted the fierce tiger and stole its spirit -- brave men with fierce hearts, stripped of boldness, fell back of themselves and dared not show disrespect to their lord.
translations.idiomatic: Silian, a mere scholar attending a weak prince, boldly proclaimed the greater duty, broke the fierce tiger's spirit, and left hardened warriors shaken and retreating, unable to offer insult to their lord.

sentences.zh: 誠使有國家者舉不失義，天下其何以抗之哉？

translations.literal: If truly those who hold a state acted without failing in righteousness, how could the realm resist them?
translations.idiomatic: If rulers truly never failed in righteousness, how could the realm stand against them?

sentences.zh: 宜太宗之尊表云。

translations.literal: No wonder Taizong held him in high regard, as the inscription says.
translations.idiomatic: Small wonder Taizong honored him so, as the inscription records.

sentences.zh: 璹字令璋，少孤，撫昆媦友愛。

translations.literal: Shu, courtesy name Lingzhang, was orphaned young; he nurtured his elder and younger siblings with affection.
translations.idiomatic: Shu, courtesy name Lingzhang, lost his parents young and raised his brothers and sisters with tender care.

sentences.zh: 力學，才辯掞邁。

translations.literal: He studied hard; his talent and eloquence outstripped others.
translations.idiomatic: He studied tirelessly, and his talent and eloquence surpassed his peers.

sentences.zh: 永徽中，舉明經第，補太子宮門郎。

translations.literal: In the Yonghui era he passed the Mingjing examination and was appointed Gate Officer of the Heir Apparent's palace.
translations.idiomatic: During Yonghui he passed the Mingjing examination and became gate officer in the heir apparent's palace.

sentences.zh: 以論撰勞，進秘書郎。

translations.literal: For labor in compilation he was promoted to Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: For his work on historical compilation he was promoted to secretary.

sentences.zh: 稍遷中書舍人，封吳興縣男。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Drafting Secretary and enfeoffed as Baron of Wuxing County.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to drafting secretary and was enfeoffed as Baron of Wuxing County.

sentences.zh: 武后時，擢夏官侍郎。

translations.literal: Under Empress Wu he was raised to Vice Minister of the Summer Office.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu he was promoted to vice minister of the Summer Office.

sentences.zh: 坐從弟敬節叛，貶桂州長史。

translations.literal: Because his cousin Jingjie rebelled, he was demoted to chief administrator of Gui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When his cousin Jingjie rebelled, he was demoted to chief administrator of Gui Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 后方以符瑞自神，璹取山川草樹名有「武」字者，以為上應國姓，裒類以聞。

translations.literal: Later the Empress was deifying herself through omens; Shu gathered names of mountains, rivers, grasses, and trees containing the character "Wu," holding them a celestial match for the dynastic surname, collected them by category, and reported them.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as the empress sought to prove her divinity through omens, Shu collected names of mountains, rivers, plants, and trees containing the character "Wu," took them as heaven's answer to the dynastic surname, sorted them by kind, and reported them.

sentences.zh: 后大悅，拜檢校天官侍郎，擢文昌左丞、同鳳閣鸞臺平章事。

translations.literal: The Empress was greatly pleased; he was made Acting Vice Minister of the Celestial Office, then raised to Left Assistant of the Department of Literary Glory and Co-Drafter with concurrent duty in the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was delighted; he was made acting vice minister of the Celestial Office, then promoted to left assistant of the Department of Literary Glory and co-drafter with concurrent duty in the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.

sentences.zh: 永徽後，左右史唯對仗承旨，仗下謀議不得聞。

translations.literal: After Yonghui, the Left and Right Historians received instructions only at imperial audience; deliberations off the dais could not be heard.
translations.idiomatic: After Yonghui the left and right historians heard the emperor's will only during formal audience; deliberations off the dais went unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 璹以帝王謨訓不可闕紀，請仗下所言軍國政要，責宰相自撰，號《時政記》，以授史官。

translations.literal: Shu held that the monarch's policies and teachings must not go unrecorded; he requested that military and state essentials spoken off the dais be compiled by the chancellor himself, titled 《Records of Current Governance》, and handed to the historiographers.
translations.idiomatic: Shu argued that the ruler's counsels must not be left unrecorded and asked that military and state matters discussed off the dais be written up by the chancellor himself under the title 《Records of Current Governance》 and given to the historiographers.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: [The court] followed his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved his proposal.

sentences.zh: 時政有記自璹始。

translations.literal: Records of current governance began with Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The keeping of records of current governance began with Shu.

sentences.zh: 坐事，降司賓少卿。

translations.literal: For an offense he was demoted to Vice Director of the Office of Reception.
translations.idiomatic: After an offense he was demoted to vice director of the Office of Reception.

sentences.zh: 延載初，拜納言，有司以璹族犯法，不可為侍臣者，璹曰：「王敦犯順，導典樞機；

translations.literal: At the start of Yanzai he was made Chief Speaker; the relevant offices argued that because Shu's clan had violated the law he could not serve as palace attendant; Shu said: "Wang Dun rose in rebellion, yet Dao held the secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yanzai he was made chief speaker; the relevant offices argued that because members of Shu's clan had broken the law he could not serve at court; Shu said, "Wang Dun rebelled, yet Wang Dao held the secretariat;

sentences.zh: 嵇康被戮，紹以忠死。

translations.literal: Ji Kang was executed, yet Shan Tao died in loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Kang was put to death, yet Shan Tao remained loyal unto death.

sentences.zh: 是能為累乎？

translations.literal: Can such things truly burden a man?
translations.idiomatic: Can kinship truly be held against a man?

sentences.zh: 」后曰：「此朕意，卿無恤浮言。

translations.literal: " The Empress said: "This is my intention; do not heed loose talk.
translations.idiomatic: " The empress said, "This is my wish; pay no heed to idle talk.

sentences.zh: 證聖初，加秋官尚書。

translations.literal: At the start of Zhensheng he was given the additional title Minister of the Autumn Office.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Zhensheng he was given the additional title minister of the Autumn Office.

sentences.zh: 明堂火，后欲避正殿，應天變。

translations.literal: The Bright Hall caught fire; the Empress wished to vacate the main hall to respond to the celestial change.
translations.idiomatic: When the Bright Hall burned, the empress wished to leave the main hall to answer heaven's warning.

sentences.zh: 璹奏：「此人火，非天災也。

translations.literal: Shu memorialized: "This was a fire caused by men, not a disaster from Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Shu memorialized, "This fire was set by men, not sent by heaven.

sentences.zh: 昔宣榭火，周世延；

translations.literal: Formerly when Xuanshe burned, the Zhou dynasty endured;
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanshe burned, the Zhou endured;

sentences.zh: 建章焚，漢業昌。

translations.literal: when Jianzhang was consumed by fire, Han's enterprise flourished.
translations.idiomatic: when Jianzhang burned, Han flourished.

sentences.zh: 且彌勒成佛，七寶臺須臾散壞。

translations.literal: Moreover when Maitreya became Buddha, the jeweled terrace crumbled in an instant.
translations.idiomatic: And when Maitreya attained buddhahood, the jeweled terrace fell apart in a moment.

sentences.zh: 聖人之道，隨物示化，況明堂布政之宮，非宗廟，不宜避正殿，貶常禮。

translations.literal: The way of sages adapts to things to show transformation; moreover the Bright Hall is a palace for proclaiming government, not an ancestral temple -- one ought not vacate the main hall and diminish regular rites.
translations.idiomatic: The sage's way transforms with circumstance; moreover the Bright Hall is a hall of government, not an ancestral temple -- one should not leave the main hall and set aside ordinary rites.

sentences.zh: 」左拾遺劉承慶曰：「明堂所以宗祀，為天所焚，當側身思過，振除前犯。

translations.literal: " Left Reminder Liu Chengqing said: "The Bright Hall is where ancestral rites are performed; burned by Heaven, one should examine oneself and repent, sweeping away prior faults.
translations.idiomatic: " Left Reminder Liu Chengqing said, "The Bright Hall is where the ruler worships his ancestors; burned by heaven, he should examine himself, repent, and cast off past faults.

sentences.zh: 」璹挾前語以傾后意。

translations.literal: " Shu wielded his earlier words to sway the Empress's intent.
translations.idiomatic: " Shu used his earlier argument to turn the empress's mind.

sentences.zh: 后乃更御端門，大酺，燕群臣，與相娛樂，遂造天樞著己功德，命璹為使，董督之。

translations.literal: The Empress then instead held court at Duangate, gave a great feast, entertained the ministers, and enjoyed herself with them; she then had the Celestial Pivot cast to record her merit and ordered Shu as commissioner to oversee it.
translations.idiomatic: The empress then held court at Duangate instead, gave a great feast, and entertained her ministers; she next had the Celestial Pivot cast to proclaim her merit and appointed Shu commissioner to supervise the work.

sentences.zh: 功費浩廣，見金不足，乃斂天下農器並鑄。

translations.literal: The work and expense were vast; finding gold insufficient, she gathered the Empire's farming tools and cast them together.
translations.idiomatic: The project was vast and costly; when gold proved insufficient, she collected farming tools from across the empire and had them cast together.

sentences.zh: 以功賜爵一級。

translations.literal: For his service he was granted one rank of nobility.
translations.idiomatic: In recognition of the work, he received one step in noble rank.

sentences.zh: 后封嵩山，詔璹總知儀注，為封禪副使。

translations.literal: When the Empress performed the fengshan rite at Mount Song, an edict made Shu general overseer of protocol and deputy commissioner for the fengshan.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress performed the fengshan rite at Mount Song, an edict made Shu general overseer of protocol and deputy commissioner for the rite.

sentences.zh: 更造明堂，又以使護作，加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When the Bright Hall was rebuilt, he again served as commissioner to supervise construction and was given the title Silver Gleaming Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: When the Bright Hall was rebuilt, he again served as commissioner supervising the work and was made Silver Gleaming Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 大食使者獻師子，璹曰：「是獸非肉不食，自碎葉至都，所費廣矣。

translations.literal: Envoys from Dashi presented a lion; Shu said: "This beast eats nothing but flesh; from Suyab to the capital the cost is vast.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys from Dashi presented a lion; Shu said, "This beast eats nothing but meat; from Suyab to the capital the expense is enormous.

sentences.zh: 陛下鷹犬且不蓄，而厚資養猛獸哉！

translations.literal: Your Majesty keeps neither hawks nor hounds -- yet would lavishly nourish a fierce beast!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty keeps neither hawks nor hounds -- yet would lavishly feed a savage beast!

sentences.zh: 」有詔大食停獻。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered Dashi to cease presenting [such gifts].
translations.idiomatic: " An edict ordered Dashi to stop sending such tribute.

sentences.zh: 時九鼎成，后欲用黃金塗之。

translations.literal: When the Nine Cauldrons were completed, the Empress wished to gild them with gold.
translations.idiomatic: When the Nine Cauldrons were finished, the empress wished to coat them with gold.

sentences.zh: 璹奏：「鼎者，神器，貴質樸，不待外飾。

translations.literal: Shu memorialized: "Cauldrons are sacred vessels; plain substance is prized -- they need no outward adornment.
translations.idiomatic: Shu memorialized, "Cauldrons are sacred vessels; their value lies in plain substance, not outward adornment.

sentences.zh: 臣觀其上先有五采雜昈，豈待塗金為符曜耶？

translations.literal: Your subject observes that they already bear five-colored marbling -- must one add gilding to make them omens of glory?
translations.idiomatic: Your subject sees that they already bear five-colored mottling -- must gold be added to make them signs of glory?

sentences.zh: 」后乃止。

translations.literal: " The Empress then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: " The empress then abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 契丹李盡忠盜塞，副梁王武三思為榆關道安撫使。

translations.literal: When the Khitan Li Jinzhong raided the frontier, [Shu] served as deputy to the Prince of Liang Wu Sansi, Pacification Commissioner of the Yuguan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan Li Jinzhong raided the frontier, Shu served as deputy to the Prince of Liang Wu Sansi, pacification commissioner of the Yuguan circuit.

sentences.zh: 坐累，下遷益州長史。

translations.literal: For implicated guilt he was demoted to chief administrator of Yi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Because of the affair he was demoted to chief administrator of Yi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 始，蜀吏貪暴，璹擿發之，無所容貸。

translations.literal: At first Shu officials in Shu were greedy and violent; Shu exposed them and showed no leniency.
translations.idiomatic: At first the officials of Shu were greedy and brutal; Shu exposed them and showed no mercy.

sentences.zh: 后聞，降璽詔慰勞，因謂左右曰：「為二千石清其身者易，使吏盡清者難，唯璹為兼之。

translations.literal: When the Empress heard, she sent an imperial edict of consolation and told those beside her: "For a two-thousand-dan official to keep himself clean is easy; to make every subordinate official clean is hard -- only Shu has achieved both.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress heard of it, she sent an imperial edict of praise and told those around her, "For a two-thousand-dan official to keep himself clean is easy; to make every subordinate clean is hard -- only Shu has done both.

sentences.zh: 」新都丞硃待辟坐贓應死，待辟所厚浮屠理中謀殺璹，據劍南。

translations.literal: " The assistant magistrate of Xindu, Zhu Daibi, was guilty of embezzlement and deserved death; a monk named Lizhong whom Daibi had favored plotted to kill Shu and seize the Sword South.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhu Daibi, assistant magistrate of Xindu, had embezzled funds and deserved death; a monk named Lizhong whom he had patronized plotted to kill Shu and seize control of the Sword South.

sentences.zh: 有密告后者，詔璹窮按。

translations.literal: Someone secretly reported this to the Empress; an edict ordered Shu to investigate thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: Someone secretly reported the plot to the empress, and an edict ordered Shu to investigate it to the end.

sentences.zh: 璹深探其獄，跡疑似皆捕逮，株黨牽聯數千人。

translations.literal: Shu dug deep into the case; anyone even slightly implicated was arrested; through clan ties and association, several thousand were entangled.
translations.idiomatic: Shu pressed the case relentlessly; anyone even remotely implicated was arrested, and clan ties and associations swept up several thousand people.

sentences.zh: 獄具，后遣洛州長史宋玄爽、御史中丞霍獻可覆視，無所翻，坐沒入五十餘族，知反流徙者什八以上，道路冤噪。

translations.literal: When the case was complete, the Empress sent Luoyang chief administrator Song Xuanshuang and Censor-in-Chief Huo Xianke to review it; nothing was overturned; more than fifty clans were confiscated and banished; those knowingly banished exceeded eight in ten; the roads resounded with wrongful lament.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was closed, the empress sent Luoyang chief administrator Song Xuanshuang and censor-in-chief Huo Xianke to review it; nothing was overturned; more than fifty clans were confiscated and banished, and well over eight in ten of those exiled knew themselves innocent; the roads rang with cries of injustice.

sentences.zh: 監察御史袁恕己劾奏璹獄不平，有詔勿治。

translations.literal: Supervising Censor Yuan Shuji memorialized impeaching that Shu's case was unjust; an edict ordered that it not be pursued.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising censor Yuan Shuji impeached Shu for an unjust case, but an edict ordered that the matter not be pursued.

sentences.zh: 召拜地官、冬官二尚書。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed concurrently Minister of the Earth Office and Minister of the Winter Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed concurrently minister of the Earth Office and minister of the Winter Office.

sentences.zh: 久之，致仕。

translations.literal: After a long time he retired.
translations.idiomatic: In time he retired.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十四，遺令薄葬。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-four; his final instruction was for a simple burial.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-four and left instructions for a plain burial.

sentences.zh: 贈越州都督，諡曰成。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Area Commander of Yue Prefecture; posthumous name Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made area commander of Yue Prefecture and given the posthumous name Cheng.

sentences.zh: 孫 珽弟珽。

translations.literal: Younger brother Ting.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother was Ting.

sentences.zh: 珽篤學有立志，擢明經。

translations.literal: Ting studied devotedly and had firm resolve; he passed the Mingjing examination.
translations.idiomatic: Ting studied with devotion and strong purpose and passed the Mingjing examination.

sentences.zh: 歷六州刺史，政皆有績，數被褒賜，累封宣城郡公。

translations.literal: He served as prefect of six prefectures; in each his governance showed merit; he was repeatedly praised and rewarded; and was in succession enfeoffed as Duke of Xuancheng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of six prefectures, governing well in each; he was repeatedly praised and rewarded, and was eventually enfeoffed as Duke of Xuancheng Commandery.

sentences.zh: 遷太子詹事，兼左庶子。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, concurrently serving as Left Subordinate to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, concurrently serving as Left Subordinate to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 時節湣太子稍失道，珽凡四上書諫。

translations.literal: At that time the Jiemin Crown Prince was gradually straying from the Way; Ting altogether submitted four memorials admonishing him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Crown Prince Jiemin was gradually straying from proper conduct, and Ting submitted four memorials admonishing him.

sentences.zh: 其一曰：「臣聞賈誼稱『選天下端士，使與太子居處出入，故太子見正事，聞正言，行正道，左右前後皆正人也。

translations.literal: The first said: "Your subject has heard that Jia Yi stated, 'Select upright gentlemen from throughout the realm and have them dwell, go out, and come in with the Heir Apparent—thus the Heir Apparent sees upright affairs, hears upright words, walks the upright path, and those to his left and right, before and behind, are all upright men.
translations.idiomatic: The first read: "Your subject has heard Jia Yi say, 'Choose upright men from throughout the realm to live with the Heir Apparent, going out and coming in with him—so that the Heir Apparent sees what is right, hears what is right, and acts rightly, with upright men on every side.

sentences.zh: 夫習與正人居，不能無正；

translations.literal: For one who habitually associates with upright men cannot but be without uprightness;
translations.idiomatic: For those who habitually keep company with upright men cannot fail to become upright;

sentences.zh: 習與不正人居，不能無不正。

translations.literal: one who habitually associates with unupright men cannot but be without unuprightness.
translations.idiomatic: and those who habitually keep company with unupright men cannot fail to become unupright.

sentences.zh: 教得而左右正，則太子正；

translations.literal: If instruction is obtained and those at left and right are upright, then the Heir Apparent is upright;
translations.idiomatic: If he is well taught and those around him are upright, the Heir Apparent will be upright;

sentences.zh: 太子正，天下定矣』。

translations.literal: if the Heir Apparent is upright, the realm is settled.'
translations.idiomatic: and if the Heir Apparent is upright, the realm will be secure.'

sentences.zh: 伏見內置作坊，諸工伎得入宮闈之內、禁衛之所，或言語內出，或事狀外通，小人無知，因為詐偽，有玷盛德。

translations.literal: Prostrate, I observe that within there are established workshops; various artisans and craftsmen are permitted to enter within the inner palace and the places of forbidden guard—some with words issued outward from within, some with matters and conditions communicated outward from within; petty men, lacking knowledge, thereby commit fraud and falsehood, staining your lofty virtue.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly observe that workshops have been set up within the palace, allowing artisans to enter the inner quarters and guarded precincts—some passing word from inside outward, some relaying affairs from within to the outside. Ignorant petty men take advantage of this to commit fraud, tarnishing your exalted virtue.

sentences.zh: 臣望悉出宮內造作付所司。

translations.literal: Your subject hopes that all manufacture within the palace may be moved out and entrusted to the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that all palace manufacture be moved outside and assigned to the proper offices.

sentences.zh: 其二曰：「漢文帝身弋綈，足草舄。

translations.literal: The second said: "Emperor Wen of Han personally wore coarse silk for summer; on his feet were straw sandals.
translations.idiomatic: The second read: "Emperor Wen of Han wore plain summer silk himself and straw sandals on his feet.

sentences.zh: 齊高帝闌檻用銅者，皆易以鐵。

translations.literal: The balustrades of Qi Gaodi that used bronze—all were replaced with iron.
translations.idiomatic: Gaodi of Qi replaced every bronze balustrade with iron.

sentences.zh: 經侯帶玉具劍、環佩以過魏太子，太子不視。

translations.literal: The Earl of Jing wore a sword with jade fittings and ring ornaments and pendants as he passed the Wei Heir Apparent; the Heir Apparent did not look.
translations.idiomatic: The Earl of Jing passed the Wei Heir Apparent wearing a sword with jade fittings and ring pendants; the Heir Apparent did not even glance at him.

sentences.zh: 經侯曰：『魏國亦有寶乎？

translations.literal: The Earl of Jing said, 'Does Wei also have treasures?
translations.idiomatic: The Earl of Jing asked, 'Does Wei possess any treasures?

sentences.zh: 』太子曰：『主信臣忠，魏之寶也。

translations.literal: ' The Heir Apparent said, 'When the lord trusts and ministers are loyal—that is Wei's treasure.
translations.idiomatic: ' The Heir Apparent replied, 'When the ruler is trusted and ministers are loyal—that is Wei's treasure.

sentences.zh: 』經侯委劍佩去，杜門不出。

translations.literal: ' The Earl of Jing cast aside sword and pendants and departed; he shut his door and did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: ' The Earl of Jing cast aside his sword and pendants and left; he shut his door and never ventured out again.

sentences.zh: 夫聖賢以簡素為貴，皇王以菲薄為德，惟殿下留心恭儉，損省玩好，以訓天下。

translations.literal: Sages and worthies take simplicity and plainness as prized; emperors and kings take frugality and meagerness as virtue—Your Highness alone should give mind to reverence and thrift, reduce and cut back playthings and delights, to instruct the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Sages and worthies prize simplicity; emperors and kings take frugality as virtue. I pray Your Highness attend to reverence and thrift, curtail luxury and amusements, and thereby teach the realm.

sentences.zh: 其三曰：「前世東宮門閤，往來皆有簿籍。

translations.literal: The third said: "In former times at the Eastern Palace gate office, all coming and going had registers.
translations.idiomatic: The third read: "In former times, all traffic through the Eastern Palace gate office was recorded in ledgers.

sentences.zh: 殿下時有所須，唯門司宣令，奸偽乘之，因緣增損。

translations.literal: When Your Highness occasionally had need of something, only the gate officer proclaimed the order—but treachery and falsehood seized the opportunity, increasing or decreasing as occasion arose.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Highness required something, only the gate officer should issue the order—but fraudsters seized the opportunity to inflate or reduce orders at will.

sentences.zh: 近呂升之乃代署宣敕，賴殿下糾發其奸。

translations.literal: Recently Lu Shengzhi personally signed and issued proclamations and edicts in another's stead; thanks to Your Highness exposing and bringing forth his treachery.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Lu Shengzhi took it upon himself to sign and issue edicts in Your Highness's name; only thanks to Your Highness exposing his fraud was the matter brought to light.

sentences.zh: 以後墨令及覆事，並請內印畫署，冀免詐繆。

translations.literal: Henceforth, written orders and reply reports alike—I ask that they all receive the inner seal and signature, hoping to avoid fraud and error.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, for all written orders and reply reports, I ask that Your Highness affix your personal seal and signature, so as to prevent fraud and error.

sentences.zh: 其四曰：「聖人不專其德，賢智必有所師。

translations.literal: The fourth said: "Sages do not monopolize their virtue; the worthy and wise must have someone from whom they learn.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth read: "Even sages do not rely on virtue alone; the worthy and wise must have teachers.

sentences.zh: 今司經無學士，供奉無侍讀。

translations.literal: Now the Office of the Classics has no academicians; the Supply Service has no Lecturers-in-Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: At present the Office of the Classics has no academicians, and the Supply Service has no Lecturers-in-Attendance.

sentences.zh: 宜視膳時奏請其人，俾奉講勸。

translations.literal: At the time of presenting meals one should memorialize and request the appropriate persons, causing them to attend with lecturing and admonition.
translations.idiomatic: At mealtimes Your Highness should request suitable men to attend, that they may lecture and offer counsel.

sentences.zh: 夫經所以立行修身，史所以諳識成敗，斯急務也。

translations.literal: The Classics are how one establishes conduct and cultivates the person; histories are how one becomes well acquainted with success and failure—these are urgent matters.
translations.idiomatic: The Classics teach how to conduct oneself and cultivate character; history teaches how to recognize success and failure—these are urgent priorities.

sentences.zh: 」太子雖稱善，不能用其言。

translations.literal: " Though the Heir Apparent praised them as good, he could not employ his words.
translations.idiomatic: " The Heir Apparent praised the advice but did not act on it.

sentences.zh: 及敗，索宮中，得珽諫書，中宗嘉歎。

translations.literal: When he met defeat, a search was made within the palace; Ting's admonitory memorials were found, and Zhongzong praised and sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince's plot failed, a search of the palace turned up Ting's memorials of admonition; Emperor Zhongzong praised them with admiration.

sentences.zh: 時宮臣皆得罪，獨珽擢右散騎常侍，遷秘書監。

translations.literal: At the time all palace officials were found guilty; Ting alone was promoted to Right Regular Attendant of the Cavalry and transferred to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the other palace officials were all punished, Ting alone was promoted to Right Regular Attendant of the Cavalry and appointed Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 睿宗立，拜戶部尚書。

translations.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, he was appointed Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong ascended the throne, he was appointed Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 所歷定州刺史、尚書官，皆與璹相繼云。

translations.literal: The offices he had passed through—Prefect of Dingzhou and Ministerial posts—were all taken in succession by Shu, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: The posts he had held—Prefect of Dingzhou and various ministerial offices—were subsequently filled in succession by Shu, it is said.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十四。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 始，曾祖察嘗撰《漢書訓纂》，而後之注《漢書》者，多竊取其義為己說，珽著《紹訓》以發明舊義云。

translations.literal: At the beginning—his great-grandfather Cha once compiled 《Instruction and Compilation for the Book of Han》; those who later annotated 《the Book of Han》 mostly stole his meanings for their own doctrines; Ting wrote 《Continuing the Instruction》 to elucidate the old meanings, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, his great-grandfather Cha had compiled 《Instruction and Compilation for the Book of Han》; later annotators of 《the Book of Han》 often appropriated his ideas as their own. Ting wrote 《Continuing the Instruction》 to clarify the original meanings, it is said.

sentences.zh: 令狐德棻令狐德棻，宜州華原人。

translations.literal: Linghu Defen—Linghu Defen was a native of Huayuan in Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Defen was a native of Huayuan in Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 父熙，隋鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: His father Xi was Chief Minister for Dependencies under the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xi served the Sui as Chief Minister for Dependencies.

sentences.zh: 其先乃燉煌右姓。

translations.literal: His ancestors were a prominent clan of Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: His family was a prominent clan of Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 德棻博貫文史。

translations.literal: Defen was broadly versed in literature and history.
translations.idiomatic: Defen was thoroughly versed in literature and history.

sentences.zh: 大業末，為藥城長，屬亂，不就官。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daye era he was magistrate of Yaocheng; chaos ensued, and he did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daye reign he was appointed magistrate of Yaocheng, but when chaos erupted he declined to serve.

sentences.zh: 淮安王神通據太平宮起兵，立總管府，署德棻府記室。

translations.literal: Prince of Huai'an Li Shentong seized the Taiping Palace and raised troops, established a chief directorate, and appointed Defen Secretariat Officer of the directorate.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Huai'an Li Shentong seized the Taiping Palace and raised an army, establishing a chief directorate, he appointed Defen as its secretariat officer.

sentences.zh: 高祖入關，引直大丞相府記室。

translations.literal: When Gaozu entered the Pass, he was summoned to serve directly as Secretariat Officer of the Grand Chancellor's Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu entered the Pass, he was summoned to serve as secretariat officer in the Grand Chancellor's Office.

sentences.zh: 武德初，為起居舍人，遷秘書丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude he was appointed Attendant of Daily Records; he was transferred to Assistant Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Wude reign he was appointed Attendant of Daily Records, then promoted to Assistant Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗問：「丈夫冠，婦人髻，比高大，何邪？

translations.literal: The Emperor once asked: "Men's caps and women's coiffures—compared, the coiffure is taller; why is this?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor once asked, "Men wear caps and women wear coiffures—yet the coiffure stands higher. Why is that?

sentences.zh: 」德棻對曰：「冠髻在首，君之象也。

translations.literal: " Defen replied: "Cap and coiffure are on the head—the emblem of the lord.
translations.idiomatic: " Defen replied, "The cap and coiffure sit upon the head—they symbolize the ruler.

sentences.zh: 晉之將亡，君弱臣強，故江左士女，衣小而裳大。

translations.literal: When Jin was about to perish, the lord was weak and ministers strong; therefore men and women east of the Yangzi had small upper garments and large lower garments.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin dynasty was near collapse, rulers were weak and ministers strong; thus in the lands south of the Yangzi, men's and women's upper garments grew small while their lower garments grew large.

sentences.zh: 宋武帝受命，君德尊嚴，衣裳隨亦變改。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Song received the Mandate, the lord's virtue was honored and august; garments and robes accordingly also changed.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Song received the Mandate, royal authority was restored—and fashions changed accordingly.

sentences.zh: 此近事驗也。

translations.literal: This is verified by recent events.
translations.idiomatic: Recent history confirms this.

sentences.zh: 」帝然之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 方是時，大亂後，經藉亡散，秘書湮缺，德棻始請帝重購求天下遺書，置吏稱錄。

translations.literal: Just at this time, after the great chaos, classics and records were lost and scattered; the secretariat archives were submerged and deficient; Defen first requested that the Emperor heavily purchase and seek lost books throughout the realm, establishing clerks styled Recorders.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, after the great upheaval, classical texts had been lost and scattered and the imperial archives lay in ruins. Defen was the first to ask the Emperor to purchase lost books throughout the realm at generous prices, appointing clerks to catalog them.

sentences.zh: 不數年，圖典略備。

translations.literal: Within a few years, charts and canons were largely complete.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years, the archives were largely restored.

sentences.zh: 又建言：「近代無正史，梁、陳、齊文籍猶可據，至周、隋事多脫損。

translations.literal: He further submitted a proposal: "In recent times there are no standard histories; the textual records of Liang, Chen, and Qi can still be relied upon—but as for Zhou and Sui, many affairs are lost and damaged.
translations.idiomatic: He further memorialized the throne: "In recent times we lack official histories. Records of the Liang, Chen, and Qi still survive, but much of Zhou and Sui history has been lost or damaged.

sentences.zh: 今耳目尚相及，史有所馮；

translations.literal: Now eyes and ears still reach one another; history has something upon which to rely;
translations.idiomatic: Witnesses to these events still live among us, and history still has sources to draw upon;

sentences.zh: 一易世，事皆汩暗，無所掇拾。

translations.literal: once a generation changes, affairs all sink into darkness—with nothing to gather and collect.
translations.idiomatic: but once another generation passes, these affairs will sink into obscurity, with nothing left to recover.

sentences.zh: 陛下受禪于隋，隋承周，二祖功業多在周，今不論次，各為一王史，則先烈世庸不光明，後無傳焉。

translations.literal: Your Majesty received the abdication from Sui; Sui succeeded Zhou—the achievements of both founding ancestors largely lie in Zhou; if now without ordering the sequence each is made a separate dynastic history, then the former worthies' ordinary deeds will not be illuminated, and posterity will have no tradition.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty received the throne from the Sui, which in turn succeeded the Zhou—the achievements of both founding houses lay chiefly in the Zhou era. If we fail to compile these in proper sequence, treating each as a separate dynastic history, the deeds of our forebears will go unrecorded and posterity will be left without a heritage.

sentences.zh: 」帝謂然。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said it was so.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 於是詔中書令蕭瑀、給事中王敬業、著作郎殷聞禮主魏，中書令封德彝、舍人顏師古主隋，大理卿崔善為、中書舍人孔紹安、太子洗馬蕭德言主梁，太子詹事裴矩、吏部郎中祖孝孫，秘書丞魏征主齊，秘書監竇璡、給事中歐陽詢、文學姚思廉主陳，侍中陳叔達、大史令庾儉及德棻主周。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict was issued: Grand Counselor Xiao Yu, Supervising Secretary Wang Jingye, and Compilation Officer Yin Wenli were put in charge of Wei; Grand Counselor Feng Deyi and Attendant Yan Shigu were put in charge of Sui; Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review Cui Shanwei, Secretariat Attendant Kong Shao'an, and Groom of the Heir Apparent Xiao Deyan were put in charge of Liang; Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent Pei Ju, Bureau Director of the Ministry of Personnel Zu Xiaosun, and Secretariat Assistant Wei Zheng were put in charge of Qi; Director of the Secretariat Dou Jin, Supervising Secretary Ouyang Xun, and Literary Scholar Yao Silian were put in charge of Chen; Vice Censor Chen Shuda, Grand Astrologer Yu Jian, and Defen were put in charge of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Emperor issued an edict appointing Grand Counselor Xiao Yu, Supervising Secretary Wang Jingye, and Compilation Officer Yin Wenli to compile the Wei history; Grand Counselor Feng Deyi and Attendant Yan Shigu for the Sui history; Chief Judge Cui Shanwei, Secretariat Attendant Kong Shao'an, and Groom of the Heir Apparent Xiao Deyan for the Liang history; Grand Mentor Pei Ju, Bureau Director Zu Xiaosun, and Secretariat Assistant Wei Zheng for the Qi history; Director of the Secretariat Dou Jin, Supervising Secretary Ouyang Xun, and Literary Scholar Yao Silian for the Chen history; and Vice Censor Chen Shuda, Grand Astrologer Yu Jian, and Defen for the Zhou history.

sentences.zh: 整振論譔，多歷年不能就，罷之。

translations.literal: They put in order and stirred discussion and compilation; many years passed without completion—it was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The project was organized and drafting commenced, but after many years remained unfinished and was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 貞觀三年，復詔撰定。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenguan, an edict again ordered compilation and determination.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenguan, the Emperor again ordered the histories compiled.

sentences.zh: 議者以魏有魏收、魏澹二家，書為已詳，惟五家史當立。

translations.literal: Those in discussion held that for Wei there were the two houses of Wei Shou and Wei Dan—the books were already detailed; only the histories of the five houses should be established.
translations.idiomatic: Those deliberating held that Wei was already well covered by the histories of Wei Shou and Wei Dan; only the histories of the other five dynasties needed to be written.

sentences.zh: 德棻更與秘書郎岑文本、殿中侍御史崔仁師次周史，中書舍人李百藥次齊史，著作郎姚思廉次梁、陳二史，秘書監魏征次隋史，左僕射房玄齡總監。

translations.literal: Defen again, together with Secretariat Officer Cen Wenben and Palace Censor Cui Renshi, compiled the Zhou history in sequence; Secretariat Attendant Li Baiyao compiled the Qi history in sequence; Compilation Officer Yao Silian compiled the Liang and Chen histories in sequence; Director of the Secretariat Wei Zheng compiled the Sui history in sequence; Left Vice Director Fang Xuanling supervised overall.
translations.idiomatic: Defen worked with Secretariat Officer Cen Wenben and Palace Censor Cui Renshi on the Zhou history; Secretariat Attendant Li Baiyao on the Qi history; Compilation Officer Yao Silian on the Liang and Chen histories; Director of the Secretariat Wei Zheng on the Sui history; Left Vice Director Fang Xuanling served as chief supervisor.

sentences.zh: 脩撰之原，自德棻發之，書成，賜絹四百匹。

translations.literal: The origin of revision and compilation sprang from Defen; when the books were completed, four hundred bolts of silk were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: Defen had originated the project; when the histories were completed, he was rewarded with four hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部侍郎，兼修國史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites, concurrently revising the National History.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites, concurrently overseeing revision of the National History.

sentences.zh: 累進爵彭城縣子。

translations.literal: By successive advancement he was ennobled as Viscount of Pengcheng County.
translations.idiomatic: He was eventually ennobled as Viscount of Pengcheng County.

sentences.zh: 轉太子右庶子。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Subordinate to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Right Subordinate to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 太子承乾廢，坐除名為民。

translations.literal: When Heir Apparent Chengqian was deposed, he was punished by removal of name and made a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Chengqian was deposed, he was stripped of rank and reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 召拜雅州刺史，又坐事免。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Prefect of Yazhou; again, because of an affair, he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was later recalled and appointed Prefect of Yazhou, but was again dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 會修晉家史，房玄齡奏起之。

translations.literal: When the Jin family history came to be revised, Fang Xuanling memorialized to raise him up.
translations.idiomatic: When work began on the Jin history, Fang Xuanling memorialized to have him reinstated.

sentences.zh: 預柬凡十有八人，德棻為先進，故類例多所諏定。

translations.literal: Those selected numbered eighteen in all; Defen was the senior, and therefore categories and precedents were largely determined by consultation with him.
translations.idiomatic: Eighteen scholars were selected for the project; as the senior member, Defen largely determined its categories and precedents.

sentences.zh: 除秘書少監。

translations.literal: He was appointed Deputy Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Deputy Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 永徽初，復為禮部侍郎、弘文館學士，監修國史，遷太常卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yonghui he again served as Vice Minister of Rites and Academician of the Hongwen Library, supervised revision of the National History, and was transferred to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yonghui reign he again served as Vice Minister of Rites and Academician of the Hongwen Library, overseeing revision of the National History, and was then appointed Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 高宗嘗召宰相及弘文學士坐中華殿，問：「何脩而王？

translations.literal: Gaozong once summoned the chief ministers and Hongwen academicians to sit in the Zhonghua Hall and asked: "By what cultivation does one become king?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong once summoned the chief ministers and Hongwen academicians to the Zhonghua Hall and asked, "What path leads to kingship?

sentences.zh: 若而霸？

translations.literal: By what does one become hegemon?
translations.idiomatic: What path leads to hegemony?

sentences.zh: 又當孰先？

translations.literal: And which should come first?
translations.idiomatic: And which should take precedence?

sentences.zh: 」德棻曰：「王任德，霸任刑。

translations.literal: " Defen said: "Kingship relies on virtue; hegemony relies on punishment.
translations.idiomatic: " Defen replied, "Kingship rests on virtue; hegemony rests on punishment.

sentences.zh: 夏、殷、周純用德而王，秦專刑而霸，至漢雜用之，魏、晉以降，王霸兩失。

translations.literal: Xia, Yin, and Zhou purely used virtue and became kings; Qin exclusively used punishment and became hegemon; down to Han both were used in mixture; from Wei and Jin onward, kingship and hegemony were both lost.
translations.idiomatic: Xia, Yin, and Zhou ruled through virtue alone; Qin achieved hegemony through punishment alone; Han mixed the two approaches; from Wei and Jin onward, the realm lost both true kingship and true hegemony.

sentences.zh: 若用之，王為先，而莫難焉。

translations.literal: If one is to employ them, kingship comes first—and nothing is more difficult.
translations.idiomatic: If both are to be used, kingship must come first—and nothing is harder to achieve.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「今茲何為而要？

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "For the present, what is essential?
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor asked, "What is most essential for governance today?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「古者為政，清心簡事為本。

translations.literal: " He replied: "In antiquity, in administering affairs, purifying the heart and simplifying affairs was fundamental.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "In antiquity, good governance rested on a clear mind and simplified administration.

sentences.zh: 今天下無虞，年谷豐衍，惟薄賦斂、省征役為要。

translations.literal: Now the realm is without worry; yearly grain is abundant and overflowing—only lightening levies and taxes and reducing corvée and service is essential.
translations.idiomatic: Now the realm is at peace and harvests are plentiful—the priority should be reducing taxes and lightening corvée.

sentences.zh: 」又問禹、湯、桀、紂所以興亡，對曰：「《傳》稱：『禹、湯罪己，其興也勃焉；

translations.literal: " He further asked about the reasons Yu, Tang, Jie, and Zhou rose and fell; he replied: "《The Commentary》 states: 'Yu and Tang blamed themselves—their rise was sudden;
translations.idiomatic: " He then asked why Yu, Tang, Jie, and Zhou had risen and fallen. Defen replied, "《The Commentary》 says, 'Yu and Tang blamed themselves, and their rise was swift;

sentences.zh: 桀、紂罪人，其亡也忽焉。

translations.literal: Jie and Zhou blamed others—their fall was sudden.
translations.idiomatic: Jie and Zhou blamed others, and their fall was sudden.

sentences.zh: 』然二主惑嬖色，戮諫者，造砲烙之刑，此所以亡也。

translations.literal: ' Yet the two lords were deluded by favorite colors, executed remonstrators, and created the punishment of the burning pillar—this is why they perished.
translations.idiomatic: ' Yet these two rulers were seduced by favorites, executed those who remonstrated with them, and invented the burning-pillar torture—this is why they fell.

sentences.zh: 」帝悅，厚賜以答其言。

translations.literal: " The Emperor was pleased and richly rewarded him to answer his words.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor was pleased and richly rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 遷國子祭酒、崇賢館學士，爵為公。
