translations.literal: He was transferred to Rector of the Directorate of Education and Academician of the Chongxian Library; his noble rank was made Duke.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Rector of the Directorate of Education and Academician of the Chongxian Library, with the rank of duke.

sentences.zh: 以金紫光祿大夫致仕。

translations.literal: He retired with the title of Grand Master of Golden Light and Purple Radiance.
translations.idiomatic: He retired bearing the title Grand Master of Golden Light and Purple Radiance.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十四，諡曰憲。

translations.literal: He died at eighty-four; his posthumous title was Xian.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty-four and was posthumously titled Xian.

sentences.zh: 時又有鄧世隆、顧胤、李延壽、李仁實皆以史學稱當世。

translations.literal: At the time there were also Deng Shilong, Gu Yin, Li Yanshou, and Li Renshi—all were famed in their generation for historiography.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Deng Shilong, Gu Yin, Li Yanshou, and Li Renshi were also renowned for historical scholarship.

sentences.zh: 鄧世隆鄧世隆者，相州人。

translations.literal: Deng Shilong—Deng Shilong was a native of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Shilong was a native of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 隋大業末，王世充兄子太戍河陽，引為賓客。

translations.literal: At the end of Sui Daye, Wang Shichong's brother's son Tai garrisoned Heyang and brought him in as a guest.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Sui, Wang Shichong's nephew Tai was garrisoned at Heyang and took him on as a retainer.

sentences.zh: 秦王攻洛陽，遺書諭太，世隆報書誇慢。

translations.literal: When Prince of Qin attacked Luoyang, he sent a letter instructing Tai; Shilong replied with a letter that was boastful and insolent.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Qin besieged Luoyang, he sent Tai a letter of exhortation; Shilong drafted Tai's reply in boastful, insolent terms.

sentences.zh: 洛陽平，亡命，變姓名，號隱玄先生，棲白鹿山。

translations.literal: When Luoyang was pacified, he fled and changed name and surname, styled himself Master Yinxuan, and dwelt on Mount Bailu.
translations.idiomatic: When Luoyang fell, he fled, changed his name, styled himself Master Yinxuan, and withdrew to Mount Bailu.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，召授國子主簿，與崔仁師、慕容善行、劉顗、庾安禮、敬播俱為修史學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was summoned and appointed Principal Clerk of the Directorate of Education; together with Cui Renshi, Murong Shanxing, Liu Yi, Yu Anli, and Jing Bo he all served as Academicians for Historical Revision.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhenguan reign he was summoned and appointed Principal Clerk of the Directorate of Education, serving alongside Cui Renshi, Murong Shanxing, Liu Yi, Yu Anli, and Jing Bo as an Academician for Historical Revision.

sentences.zh: 世隆內負罪，居不聊。

translations.literal: Shilong inwardly bore guilt; in dwelling he was not at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong felt guilty at heart and lived in unease.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣房玄齡諭曰：「爾為太作書，各忠其主耳。

translations.literal: Taizong sent Fang Xuanling to instruct him, saying: "You wrote the letter for Tai—each was loyal to his lord, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sent Fang Xuanling to reassure him: "You wrote that letter for Tai—each man was merely loyal to his own master.

sentences.zh: 我為天子，尚甘心匹夫邪？

translations.literal: I am Son of Heaven—would I still be willing to grudge a common man?
translations.idiomatic: I am Emperor—would I hold a grudge against a humble subject?

sentences.zh: 毋有後疑！

translations.literal: Do not harbor later doubts!
translations.idiomatic: Have no further misgivings!

sentences.zh: 」改著作佐郎，歷衛尉丞。

translations.literal: " He was changed to Assistant Compilation Officer; he passed through Vice Commandant of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: " He was appointed Assistant Compilation Officer and later served as Vice Commandant of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 初，帝以武功定天下，晚始向學，多屬文賦詩，天格贍麗，意悟沖邁。

translations.literal: At the beginning, the Emperor by martial achievement settled the realm; only late did he turn to learning; he often entrusted others with composing rhapsodies and poems—heaven's pattern was rich and ornate, his intent and insight lofty and far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: Early on the Emperor had conquered the realm by force of arms and turned to learning only later. He often commissioned others to compose prose and poetry; his literary taste was rich and ornate, his vision lofty and bold.

sentences.zh: 十三年，世隆上疏，請加集錄，帝謙不許。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Shilong submitted a memorial requesting that compilation and recording be added; the Emperor modestly did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Shilong submitted a memorial requesting that the Emperor's writings be collected and published; the Emperor declined out of modesty.

sentences.zh: 終著作郎。

translations.literal: He ended as Compilation Officer.
translations.idiomatic: He died serving as Compilation Officer.

sentences.zh: 顧胤顧胤，蘇州吳人。

translations.literal: Gu Yin—Gu Yin was a native of Wu in Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Yin was a native of Wu in Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 父覽，仕隋秘書學士。

translations.literal: His father Lan served the Sui as Academic Scholar of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lan served the Sui as a Secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 胤，永徽中累遷起居郎，兼脩國史，以撰《太宗實錄》勞，加朝散大夫、弘文館學士。

translations.literal: Yin, in the Yonghui era, was repeatedly promoted to Diary Officer, also revising the National History; for the labor of compiling the 《Veritable Records of Taizong》, he was given Gentleman Consultant for Miscellaneous Services and made Academician of the Hongwen Institute.
translations.idiomatic: During Yonghui Yin rose through posts to Diary Officer while also revising the National History. For compiling the 《Veritable Records of Taizong》 he was promoted to Gentleman Consultant for Miscellaneous Services and made an Academician of the Hongwen Institute.

sentences.zh: 論次國史，加朝請大夫，封餘杭縣男。

translations.literal: For arranging the National History in order, he was given Gentleman Consultant for Ceremonies and enfeoffed as Viscount of Yuhang County.
translations.idiomatic: For organizing the National History he was promoted to Gentleman Consultant for Ceremonies and enfeoffed Viscount of Yuhang County.

sentences.zh: 終司文郎中。

translations.literal: He ended as Compilation Officer.
translations.idiomatic: He died serving as Compilation Officer.

sentences.zh: 子琮，武后時為天官侍郎、同鳳閣鸞臺平章事。

translations.literal: His son Cong, in the time of Empress Wu, served as Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel and Co-Decision Maker of Tongfeng Pavilion and Luantai.
translations.idiomatic: His son Cong served under Empress Wu as Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel and a Grand Chancellor of Tongfeng Pavilion and Luantai.

sentences.zh: 卒，后曰：「琮不幸，令雖不舉哀，然朕以股肱，特廢視事一日。

translations.literal: When he died, the Empress said: "Cong has met misfortune; though the law does not require mourning, yet I, as his arm and thigh, specially suspend affairs of state for one day.
translations.idiomatic: When he died the Empress said: "Cong has met with misfortune. Although the law does not require mourning, as one of my closest ministers I shall suspend court for one day.

sentences.zh: 」李延壽李延壽者，世居相州。

translations.literal: " Li Yanshou—Li Yanshou was one whose family had long resided in Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Yanshou came from a family long established in Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，累補太子典膳丞、崇賢館學士。

translations.literal: In Zhenguan, he was repeatedly appointed Vice Director of Food Service for the Heir Apparent and Academician of the Chongxian Institute.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenguan he held successive posts as Vice Director of Food Service for the Heir Apparent and Academician of the Chongxian Institute.

sentences.zh: 以脩撰勞，轉御史臺主簿，兼直國史。

translations.literal: For the labor of compiling and writing, he was transferred to Principal Clerk of the Censorate, concurrently serving in direct charge of the National History.
translations.idiomatic: For his work on historical compilation he was moved to Principal Clerk of the Censorate with concurrent duty on the National History.

sentences.zh: 初，延壽父太師，多識前世舊事，常以宋、齊、梁、陳、齊、周、隋天下參隔，南方謂北為「索虜」，北方指南為「島夷」。

translations.literal: At the beginning, Yanshou's father Taishi knew many affairs of former ages; he often noted that under Song, Qi, Liang, Chen, Qi, Zhou, and Sui the realm was divided, the south calling the north "Suolu" and the north calling the south "Daoyi."
translations.idiomatic: Early on Yanshou's father Taishi, who knew a great deal about earlier times, observed that under the Song, Northern and Southern Qi, Liang, Chen, Northern Zhou, and Sui the realm had been split: southerners called northerners "Suolu" and northerners called southerners "Daoyi."

sentences.zh: 其史于本國詳，佗國略，往往訾美失傳，思所以改正，擬《春秋》編年，刊究南北事，未成而歿。

translations.literal: The histories of each state were detailed for their own state and sparse for others; often praise and blame were lost or garbled; he thought how to correct this, proposed to follow the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》 in chronological arrangement, and investigate and settle north-south affairs—but before it was finished he died.
translations.idiomatic: Each state's histories were detailed at home and sketchy abroad, so moral judgment was often distorted or lost. He wished to set this right by following the chronicle style of the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》 in treating north and south together, but died before the work was finished.

sentences.zh: 延壽既數與論譔，所見益廣，乃追終先志。

translations.literal: Yanshou, having many times joined in discussion and composition, saw ever more broadly, and so pursued and completed his father's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Having often discussed the project with his father, Yanshou's view widened and he set out to fulfill his father's aim.

sentences.zh: 本魏登國元年，盡隋義寧二年，作本紀十二、列傳八十八，謂之《北史》；

translations.literal: From the first year of Dengguo of Wei through the second year of Yining of Sui, he made twelve Basic Annals and eighty-eight Biographies, calling it the 《History of the North》;
translations.idiomatic: From Northern Wei's first year of Dengguo through Sui's second year of Yining he produced twelve annals and eighty-eight biographies, entitled the 《History of the North》;

sentences.zh: 本宋永初元年，盡陳禎明三年，作本紀十、列傳七十，謂之《南史》。

translations.literal: From the first year of Yongchu of Song through the third year of Zhenming of Chen, he made ten Basic Annals and seventy Biographies, calling it the 《History of the South》.
translations.idiomatic: From Liu Song's first year of Yongchu through Chen's third year of Zhenming he wrote ten annals and seventy biographies, entitled the 《History of the South》.

sentences.zh: 凡八代，合二書百八十篇，上之。

translations.literal: In all eight dynasties; combining the two works, one hundred eighty chapters—he submitted them.
translations.idiomatic: Covering eight dynasties in two works of 180 chapters, he submitted them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 其書頗有條理，刪落釀辭，過本書遠甚。

translations.literal: His book had considerable order; excising and trimming ornate phrasing, it surpassed the original books by far.
translations.idiomatic: The work was well organized, stripped of florid phrasing, and far superior to the source histories.

sentences.zh: 時人見年少位下，不甚稱其書。

translations.literal: People of the time, seeing him young in years and low in rank, did not greatly praise his book.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries, noting his youth and low rank, did not much acclaim the work.

sentences.zh: 遷符璽郎，兼脩國史，卒。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Seal Officer, concurrently revising the National History, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Seal Officer while continuing to revise the National History, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 嘗撰《太宗政典》，調露中，高宗觀之，咨美直筆，賜其家帛五十段，藏副秘閣，仍別錄以賜皇太子云。

translations.literal: He once compiled the 《Political Institutions of Taizong》; in Tiaolu, Gaozong read it, praised the straightforward brush, granted his household fifty bolts of silk, stored a copy in the Secret Archive, and additionally had a separate copy made to give the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He had also compiled the 《Political Institutions of Taizong》. In the Tiaolu era Gaozong read it, praised its honest record, and rewarded his family with fifty bolts of silk. A copy was kept in the Secret Archive and another was made for the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 李仁實李仁實，魏州頓丘人。

translations.literal: Li Renshi—Li Renshi was a native of Dunqiu in Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Renshi was a native of Dunqiu in Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 官至左史。

translations.literal: His office reached Left Historiographer.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Left Historiographer.

sentences.zh: 著《格論》、《通曆》等書，行于時。

translations.literal: He authored the 《Treatise on Standards》, the 《Comprehensive Calendar》, and other books; they circulated in his time.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the 《Treatise on Standards》, the 《Comprehensive Calendar》, and other works that circulated widely in his day.

sentences.zh: 令狐峘峘，德棻五世孫。

translations.literal: Linghu Tan—Tan was the fifth-generation descendant of Defen.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Tan was a fifth-generation descendant of Linghu Defen.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，及進士第。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao, he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Tianbao era he passed the jinshi examinations.

sentences.zh: 遇祿山亂，去隱南山豹林穀。

translations.literal: Encountering the Lushan rebellion, he left and hid in Baolin Valley in the Southern Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: When the An Lushan rebellion broke out he withdrew to Baolin Valley in the Zhongnan Mountains.

sentences.zh: 楊綰微時，數從之遊，而峘博學有口辯。

translations.literal: When Yang Guan was obscure, he often followed and associated with him; Tan was broad in learning and had gift of speech and debate.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guan often visited him when still unknown; Tan was erudite and eloquent.

sentences.zh: 綰為禮部侍郎，脩國史，薦峘，自華原尉拜右拾遺，兼史職。

translations.literal: When Guan was Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites, revising the National History, he recommended Tan; from magistrate of Huayuan he was appointed Right Reminder, concurrently holding a history post.
translations.idiomatic: When Guan became Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites and was revising the National History, he recommended Tan, who was promoted from magistrate of Huayuan to Right Reminder with a concurrent post in the historiography office.

sentences.zh: 累遷起居舍人。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Diary Officer of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Diary Officer of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 撰《玄宗實錄》，屬《起居注》亡散，峘裒掇詔策，備一朝之遺。

translations.literal: Compiling the 《Veritable Records of Emperor Xuanzong》—since the Diary Notes had been lost and scattered, Tan gathered and picked out edicts and policies, completing what remained of one reign.
translations.idiomatic: When compiling the 《Veritable Records of Emperor Xuanzong》 he found the Diary Notes lost and scattered, so Tan pieced together edicts and proclamations to preserve what remained of the reign.

sentences.zh: 自開元、天寶間名臣事多漏略，拙於取棄，不稱良史。

translations.literal: From Kaiyuan and Tianbao among famous ministers' affairs many were omitted and sketchy; clumsy in choosing and discarding—not worthy of a good historian.
translations.idiomatic: Accounts of prominent ministers of the Kaiyuan and Tianbao eras were often omitted; his selection was clumsy and the work hardly merits a good historian's name.

sentences.zh: 大曆中，以刑部員外郎判南曹。

translations.literal: In Dali, as Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice he oversaw the Southern Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dali era he served as Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice overseeing the Southern Bureau.

sentences.zh: 遷司封郎中，知制誥，兼史館脩撰。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of the Seals Section, drafted imperial edicts, and concurrently served as Historical Compiler in the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director of the Seals Section, drafted imperial edicts, and served concurrently as a compiler in the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 德宗立，詔元陵制度務極優厚，當竭帑藏奉用度。

translations.literal: When Dezong assumed the throne, an edict said that the regulations for the Yuan Mausoleum should be extremely generous; the treasury should be exhausted to supply the expenses.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong ascended the throne, an edict ordered that the late emperor's mausoleum be built with the utmost splendor, drawing freely on the treasury.

sentences.zh: 峘諫曰：「臣伏讀漢劉向論山陵之誡，良史咨欷。

translations.literal: Tan remonstrated, saying: "Your servant has read with reverence Han Liu Xiang's admonition on mountain tombs; good historians sigh in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Tan remonstrated: "I have read Liu Xiang of Han on the warning about tombs, and good historians have mournfully sighed over it.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why is that?

sentences.zh: 聖賢勤儉，不作無益。

translations.literal: Sages and worthies are diligent and frugal; they do not do what is of no benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Sages and worthies are frugal and do nothing useless.

sentences.zh: 昔舜葬蒼梧，弗變其肆；

translations.literal: Formerly Shun was buried at Cangwu and did not change his market;
translations.idiomatic: Shun was buried at Cangwu without disturbing the marketplace;

sentences.zh: 禹葬會稽，不改其列；

translations.literal: Yu was buried at Kuaiji and did not alter his rows;
translations.idiomatic: Yu was buried at Kuaiji without changing the ranks of farmers at plough;

sentences.zh: 周武葬畢陌，無丘壟處；

translations.literal: King Wu of Zhou was buried at Bimo with no mound or tomb;
translations.idiomatic: King Wu of Zhou was buried at Bimo with neither mound nor tumulus;

sentences.zh: 漢文葬霸陵，不起山墳。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Han was buried at Baling and did not raise a mountain tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Han was buried at Baling without raising a hill tomb.

sentences.zh: 禹非不忠，啟非不順，周公非不悌，景帝非不孝，其奉君親，皆以儉觳為無窮計。

translations.literal: Yu was not disloyal, Qi was not unfilial in succession, the Duke of Zhou was not undutiful to brothers, Emperor Jing was not unfilial—in serving lord and parent they all took frugality as an inexhaustible plan.
translations.idiomatic: It was not that Yu lacked loyalty, Qi lacked obedient succession, the Duke of Zhou lacked brotherly duty, or Emperor Jing lacked filial piety—they honored lord and parent by making frugality their enduring principle.

sentences.zh: 宋文公厚葬，《春秋》書華元為不臣；

translations.literal: Duke Wen of Song was buried lavishly; the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》 records Hua Yuan as disloyal subject;
translations.idiomatic: Duke Wen of Song was given a lavish burial, and the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》 marks Hua Yuan as disloyal;

sentences.zh: 桓魋為石槨，夫子以為不如速朽。

translations.literal: Huan Tui made a stone outer coffin; the Master thought it better to decay quickly.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Tui had a stone sarcophagus made, the Master said it would be better to rot away quickly.

sentences.zh: 由是觀之，有德者葬薄，無德者葬厚，章章可見。

translations.literal: From this observing, those with virtue are buried thinly, those without virtue buried thickly—clearly visible.
translations.idiomatic: From this it is plain that the virtuous are buried simply and the unvirtuous extravagantly.

sentences.zh: 陛下仁孝切於聖心，然尊親之義貴合於禮。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's benevolence and filial piety cut to the sacred heart; yet the principle of honoring parents values accord with rites.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's filial devotion is sincere, yet honoring one's parents should accord with ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 先帝遺詔，送終之制，一用儉約，不得以金銀緣飾。

translations.literal: The late emperor's testament: the regulations for seeing off the end—all use frugality and economy; gold and silver must not be used for trim and ornament.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor's testament prescribed frugal funeral arrangements and forbade gold and silver ornament.

sentences.zh: 陛下奉先志，無違物，若務優厚，是咈顧命，盩經誼，臣竊懼之。

translations.literal: Your Majesty follows the prior intent without violation; if you insist on generosity, this is disobeying the testament and unsettling canonical propriety—I privately fear it.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has honored his wishes; to pursue extravagance would disobey his dying command and violate ritual propriety, which deeply concerns me.

sentences.zh: 今赦令甫下，諸條未出，望速詔有司從遺制便。

translations.literal: Now the amnesty edict has just been issued and the various articles not yet promulgated; I hope you will quickly order the officials to follow the testament's regulations as convenient.
translations.idiomatic: The amnesty has just been issued and detailed regulations not yet promulgated; I beg that officials be ordered at once to follow the testament.

sentences.zh: 」詔答曰：「朕頃議山陵，荒哀迷謬，以違先旨。

translations.literal: " The edict replied: "We lately discussed the mountain tomb, muddled in grief and lost in error, thereby violating the prior intent.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor replied: "In my recent deliberations on the mausoleum, grief led me astray and I violated my father's intent.

sentences.zh: 卿引據典禮，非唯中朕之失，亦使朕不遺君親於患。

translations.literal: You cited canon and rites—not only hitting Our fault, but also enabling Us not to leave lord and parent in peril.
translations.idiomatic: You invoked precedent and ritual—not only correcting my error but keeping me from bringing harm upon my father even in death.

sentences.zh: 敢不聞義而從，奉以終始？

translations.literal: How dare We not, hearing righteousness, follow and uphold it to the end?
translations.idiomatic: How could I fail to heed your counsel and follow it to the end?

sentences.zh: 雖古遺直，何以加焉！

translations.literal: Even the upright remonstrators of antiquity—how could one add to this!
translations.idiomatic: Even the most forthright remonstrators of old could not surpass this!

sentences.zh: 峘在吏部，因尚書劉晏力。

translations.literal: Tan was in the Ministry of Personnel, relying on the power of Director Liu Yan.
translations.idiomatic: While in the Ministry of Personnel Tan relied on the support of Director Liu Yan.

sentences.zh: 時楊炎為侍郎，故峘內德晏，至分闕，以善闕奉晏，惡闕與炎，炎心不平。

translations.literal: At the time Yang Yan was Vice Director; therefore Tan inwardly favored Liu Yan; when dividing vacancies, good vacancies he gave to Liu Yan, bad vacancies to Yang Yan, and Yang Yan's heart was not at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan was then a vice director; Tan secretly favored Liu Yan, and when choosing appointees he gave the best posts to Yan and the worst to Yang Yan, who resented it.

sentences.zh: 建中初，峘為禮部侍郎，炎執政，不為憾。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong, Tan was Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites; Yan held power—he did not hold a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianzhong Tan became Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites; although Yang Yan was in power, he bore no grudge.

sentences.zh: 炎出故宰相杜鴻漸門下，其子封求弘文生，以托峘，峘謝使者曰：「得公手署，峘得以識。

translations.literal: Yan had come from under former Chancellor Du Hongjian; his son Feng sought a Hongwen Institute student position and entrusted Tan; Tan told the messenger: "With the Duke's own hand-signed note, Tan can recognize it.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan had studied under the former chancellor Du Hongjian; his son Feng sought admission as a Hongwen Institute student and asked Tan to help. Tan told the messenger: "With a note in your own hand I can verify the request.

sentences.zh: 」炎不疑，署送之。

translations.literal: " Yan did not suspect; he signed and sent it.
translations.idiomatic: " Yang Yan suspected nothing and signed and sent it.

sentences.zh: 峘即日奏言：「宰相迫臣以私，從之負陛下，不從則害臣。

translations.literal: Tan that same day memorialized: "The Chancellor forced your servant with private interest; to obey would fail Your Majesty, not to obey would harm your servant.
translations.idiomatic: That day Tan memorialized: "The Chancellor pressured me with a private favor—if I complied I would betray Your Majesty, if I refused he would destroy me.

sentences.zh: 」帝以詰炎，炎具道所以然。

translations.literal: " The Emperor used this to interrogate Yan; Yan fully explained the reason.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor questioned Yang Yan, who explained the whole affair.

sentences.zh: 帝怒曰：「此奸人，無可奈何！

translations.literal: The Emperor angrily said: "This treacherous man—nothing can be done about him!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said in anger: "This scoundrel is beyond remedy!

sentences.zh: 」欲殺之，炎苦救解，乃貶衡州別駕。

translations.literal: " He wished to kill him; Yan bitterly pleaded and secured release; thereupon he was demoted to Vice Prefect of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " He wanted Tan executed; Yang Yan pleaded hard for him and Tan was demoted instead to Vice Prefect of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 遷刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Regional Prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made regional prefect.

sentences.zh: 李泌執政，召拜太子右庶子，復為脩撰。

translations.literal: Li Bi held power; he was summoned and appointed Right Vice Supervisor of the Heir Apparent, again serving as compiler.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Bi took power Tan was recalled as Right Vice Supervisor of the Heir Apparent and again made a historical compiler.

sentences.zh: 性愎且介，人人與為怨。

translations.literal: His nature was obstinate and upright; everyone became his enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Obstinate and uncompromising by nature, he made an enemy of nearly everyone.

sentences.zh: 孔述睿同脩史，峘忿細故，數侵之，述睿長者，無所校。

translations.literal: Kong Shurui jointly revised history; Tan resented petty matters and repeatedly encroached on him; Shurui was a man of forbearance and made no reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Collaborating on the history with Kong Shurui, Tan picked quarrels over trifles and harried him repeatedly; Shurui, a man of forbearance, never took offense.

sentences.zh: 貞元五年，坐守衡州冒前刺史戶口為己最，竇參素惡之，貶吉州別駕，稍遷刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenyuan, on account of governing Hengzhou while falsely claiming the prior prefect's household registers as his own highest count, Dou Can who had long hated him demoted him to Vice Prefect of Jizhou; gradually he was transferred to Regional Prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 5 he was found to have credited himself with the prior prefect of Hengzhou's household register figures; Dou Can, who disliked him, had him demoted to Vice Prefect of Jizhou, then gradually promoted to prefect.

sentences.zh: 齊映為江西觀察使，按部及州。

translations.literal: Qi Ying was Jiangxi Observation Commissioner; he made a circuit inspection reaching the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Ying, as Jiangxi Observation Commissioner, toured his jurisdiction and reached Tan's prefecture.

sentences.zh: 峘輕映後出先至宰相，今雖屬刺史，自挾所以過映者，至迎謁，頗怏怏。

translations.literal: Tan looked down on Ying for being later in emergence yet earlier reaching Grand Chancellor; now though subordinate as prefect, he relied on grounds by which he surpassed Ying; when coming to greet and audience, he was quite displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Tan looked down on Qi Ying as a junior who had reached the chancellorship before him; though now Ying's subordinate as prefect, Tan counted on past grievances and showed evident displeasure when going to greet him.

sentences.zh: 以語其妻，妻曰：「君自視何如人，以白頭走小生前。

translations.literal: He told his wife; his wife said: "You yourself see what sort of man you are, running before a junior while white-haired.
translations.idiomatic: He told his wife, who said: "Consider what sort of man you are—to go cringing before a man young enough to be your son while your hair is white!

sentences.zh: 君不以比見映，雖黜死，我無憾。

translations.literal: If you do not go see Ying in this way, though demoted to death, I have no regret.
translations.idiomatic: If you refuse to demean yourself before him, even if you are demoted or die, I shall have no regrets.

sentences.zh: 」映至，峘入謁，從容步進，不襪首屬戎器，映以為恨。

translations.literal: " When Ying arrived, Tan entered for audience, walked in at ease, did not put on socks and cap and carry military arms; Ying regarded this as resentment-worthy.
translations.idiomatic: " When Qi Ying arrived Tan paid his respects but strolled in casually without proper cap and girded weapons; Ying took this as a deliberate insult.

sentences.zh: 去至府，擿峘舉奏前刺史過失無狀，不宜按部，貶衢州別駕。

translations.literal: Leaving to reach the headquarters, he picked at Tan and memorialized that the prior prefect's faults were groundless, unsuitable for circuit inspection; demoted to Vice Prefect of Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At headquarters Qi Ying charged Tan with groundlessly impeaching his predecessor and deemed him unfit to receive an inspection tour, and had him demoted to Vice Prefect of Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 刺史田敦，峘門生也，與峘昧生平，至是迎拜，分俸半以賙給之。

translations.literal: Prefect Tian Dun was Tan's gate student; with Tan he had never been acquainted in life; reaching this, he went to greet and bow, dividing half his salary to relieve and supply him.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect Tian Dun had been Tan's student though they had never met; he now came to welcome him and gave him half his salary for support.

sentences.zh: 在衢十年，順宗立，以秘書少監召，未至，卒。

translations.literal: At Qu for ten years; when Shunzong assumed the throne, he was summoned as Vice Director of the Secretariat; before arriving, he died.
translations.idiomatic: After ten years at Quzhou he was summoned as Vice Director of the Secretariat when Emperor Shunzong ascended the throne, but died before he could take up the post.

sentences.zh: 初，受詔撰《代宗實錄》，未就，會貶，詔聽在外成書。

translations.literal: At the beginning, he received an edict to compile the 《Veritable Records of Emperor Daizong》; not yet finished, he happened to be demoted; an edict permitted him to complete the book while outside [office].
translations.idiomatic: Upon receiving orders to compile the 《Veritable Records of Emperor Daizong》, he was demoted before finishing; the court allowed him to complete the work in exile.

sentences.zh: 元和中，其子太僕丞丕獻之。

translations.literal: In Yuanhe, his son Pi, Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanhe era his son Pi, Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, presented it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 以勞贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: For the labor, posthumously awarded Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: For this service Tan was posthumously made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：「文本才猷，世南鯁諤，百藥之持論，亮、思廉之邃雅，德棻之辭章，皆治世華采，而淟汩于隋，光明于唐，何哉？

translations.literal: The encomium says: "Wenben's talent and strategy, Shinan's blunt remonstrance, Baiyao's sustained arguments, Liang's and Silian's profound elegance, Defen's literary polish—all are splendor of an ordered age; yet they were fouled in Sui and bright in Tang—why?
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: "The talents of Wenben, Shinan's blunt honesty, Baiyao's principled arguments, the depth and grace of Liang and Silian, Defen's literary brilliance—all are adornments of good government; yet they were sullied under the Sui and shone under the Tang. Why?

sentences.zh: 蓋天下未嘗無賢，以不用亡；

translations.literal: Probably the realm has never lacked the worthy—they perish through non-employment;
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps the world never lacks worthy men—they are lost when not employed;

sentences.zh: 不必多賢，以見用興。

translations.literal: Not necessarily many worthies—through being seen and employed they rise.
translations.idiomatic: nor does it take many; a state flourishes when they are put to use.

sentences.zh: 夫典章圖史，有國者尤急，所以考存亡成敗，陳諸前而為之戒。

translations.literal: Now statutes, regulations, maps, and histories—for one who holds a state especially urgent—thereby examining survival and extinction, success and failure, setting them before one as warning.
translations.idiomatic: Canon law, maps, and history are especially vital to any state, for by them one weighs rise and fall and sets warnings before one's eyes.

sentences.zh: 方天下初定，德棻首發其議，而後唐之文物粲然，誠知治之本歟！

translations.literal: Just as the realm was first settled, Defen first raised this proposal; afterward Tang's cultural achievements were brilliant—truly knowing the root of good government!
translations.idiomatic: When the empire was first pacified, Defen was first to urge this, and thereafter Tang's cultural splendor unfolded—a true insight into the foundation of rule!
